ITQAN:v4p413#5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p413#5/r1.speaker: النبي
ITQAN:v4p413#5/r1.claim: Al-Hakim transmits from Ibn Umar a Prophetic report asking whether anyone can recite a thousand verses daily; the Prophet answers that one can recite Sūrat al-Takathur.
ITQAN:v4p413#5/r1.anchor: أخرج الحاكم من حديث ابن عمر مرفوعا

BURSEVI:v10p387/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p387/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p387/r1.claim: Lahw is whatever occupies someone from what matters; takathur is competing and boasting in abundance, each side claiming greater numbers.
BURSEVI:v10p387/r1.anchor: والتكاثر التباري في الكثرة والتباهي بها وأن يقول هؤلاء نحن أكثر وهؤلاء نحن أكثر

BURSEVI:v10p387/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p387/r2.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p387/r2.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says distraction turns someone toward amusement; “kept you busy” gives the result of the verb's original sense, and the omitted object is what mattered, especially religious duties.
BURSEVI:v10p387/r2.anchor: وحذف الملهى عنه أي الذي إلهي عنه وهو ما يعنيهم من أمر الدين للتعظيم والمبالغة

BURSEVI:v10p387/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p387/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p387/r3.claim: Omitting what distraction kept them from intensifies the meaning and allows every neglected religious concern to enter: remembrance, duties and recommended acts of heart and limbs.
BURSEVI:v10p387/r3.anchor: المقام مثل إلهاكم التكاثر عن ذكر الله وعن الواجبات

BURSEVI:v10p387/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p387/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p387/r4.claim: The definite article marks familiar, blameworthy competition over perishing worldly goods such as money, status, supporters, and relatives; boasting in lasting religious qualities is praiseworthy when it acknowledges God's favor.
BURSEVI:v10p387/r4.anchor: وتعريف التكاثر للعهد والعهد المذموم هو التكاثر في الأمور الدنيوية الفانية

BURSEVI:v10p387/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p387/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p387/r5.claim: Examples of permissible gratitude include al-‘Abbas boasting of the water service and Shayba of holding the Ka‘ba's key, before ‘Ali boasts of having struck at disbelief.
BURSEVI:v10p387/r5.anchor: تفاخر العباس رضي الله عنه بأن السقاية بيده وتفاخر شيبة بأن مفتاح البيت بيده

BURSEVI:v10p387/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p387/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p387/r6.claim: Takathur is reciprocal boasting: two people compare wealth or numbers, each saying he has more money and a stronger following.
BURSEVI:v10p387/r6.anchor: والتكاثر مكاثرة اثنين مالا أو عددا بأن يقول كل منهما لصاحبه أنا أكثر منك مالا

BURSEVI:v10p387/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p387/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p387/r7.claim: Banu ‘Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm competed over leaders and notable people, each claiming more prominent men; when outnumbered, Banu Sahm said earlier conflict had exhausted them, so they counted both living and dead.
BURSEVI:v10p387/r7.anchor: إن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا وتعادوا وتكاثروا بالسعادة والإشراف في الإسلام

QASHANI:102:1-4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:102:1-4/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:102:1-4/r1.claim: Rivalry in accumulation distracts people with fleeting sensory and imagined pleasures, wasting innate potential, purity, intellect, and lasting spiritual perfection for worldly boasting.
QASHANI:102:1-4/r1.anchor: اللذات الحسية والخيالية الفانية من نعيم الحياة الدنيا التي احتجبتم بها

QASHANI:102:1-4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:102:1-4/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:102:1-4/r2.claim: Competition over wealth, children, and ancestry can extend even to boasting about long-dead ancestors’ bones, driven by imagination and concealing illusion.
QASHANI:102:1-4/r2.anchor: من كثرة الأموال والأولاد وشرف الآباء والأجداد كل مذهب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r1.claim: Islahi pairs al-Takāthur with al-Qāriʿah because both address what matters in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Tak āthur forms a pair with S ūrah al-Q āri‘ah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r2.claim: Al-Qāriʿah teaches that good deeds alone weigh in the Hereafter: more good deeds bring salvation, while greater evil brings lasting doom despite worldly treasure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r2.anchor: will have weight in the Balance of Justice.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r3.claim: This sūrah warns people who spend life competing for wealth and luxuries that they will face the dreadful consequences of forgetting accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p426/r3.anchor: outdo one another in the acquisition of wealth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r1.claim: The verb alhā means to allure or deceive people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r2.claim: Takāthur means striving to outdo one another in wealth and children.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r2.anchor: means “to strive to outdo one another in wealth and children.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r3.claim: Because families secured tribal defense, the family with most members received that responsibility, spurring rivalry in both wealth and family size.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r3.anchor: a family was responsible for the defence and security of a tribe

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r4.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs took pride in surpassing others in wealth and having large families.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r4.anchor: they used to take a lot of pride in not only outdoing one another in wealth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p427/r5.claim: Modern family planning has shifted the social preference toward smaller families, yet an unlimited standard of living keeps the desire for wealth insatiable.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p428/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p428/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p428/r1.claim: Because greed grows faster than living standards, the race for material gain has no end and distracts people from the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p428/r1.anchor: unmindful to the other important realities of life

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p393/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p393/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p393/r1.claim: Qatada says people boasted that their tribe outnumbered another until they died in error.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p393/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ألهاكم التكاثر ﴾ قال قالوا نحن أكثر من بني فلان وبنو فلان أكثر من بني فلان

QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r1.claim: God's name was holy before eternity, needs no time or place in the future, and cannot be circumscribed by spatial limits.
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r1.anchor: اسم عزيز تقدس في آزاله عن كل مكان

QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r2.claim: Because no number can circumscribe God, increase or decrease cannot be attributed to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r2.anchor: لا يقطعه حد فأنى يجوز في وصفه المكان ؟ ولا يقطعه عد

QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r3.claim: People's mutual boasting occupied them through the end of their lives, until they died.

QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that they boasted of their forefathers and ancestors, celebrating the living and those who had died.

QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r5.claim: Their boasting led them to count their dead as they counted the living, and their competition in wealth and children distracted them from obedience to God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p445/r5.anchor: وأنساكم تكاثركم بالأموال والأولاد طاعة الله

SULAMI:v2p417/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p417/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p417/r1.claim: Rivalry in accumulating wealth and status distracted people from life through remembrance of their dead.
SULAMI:v2p417/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : شغلكم التكاثر بموتاكم عن الحياة بذكرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan according to all exegetes, while al-Bukhārī calls it Madinan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول جميع المفسرين. وقال البخاري: مدنية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say the rival clans of Sahm and ʿAbd Manāf counted their living notables, then their dead; ʿAbd Manāf had more living, but Sahm more dead from pre-Islamic times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r2.anchor: أنه فيما روى الكلبي ومقاتل: كان بين بني سهم وبين بني عبد مناف لحاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r3.claim: Qatada says the passage concerns Jews who claimed their tribes outnumbered other tribes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: نزلت في اليهود، قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says it concerns a clan among the Anṣār.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: نزلت في بطن من الأنصار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r5.claim: Alhākum means occupied you; under the clan-rivalry report they counted the living to exhaustion and then competed over the dead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p535/r5.anchor: ألهاكم: شغلكم فعلى ما روى الكلبي ومقاتل يكون المعنى:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r3.claim: The majority read alhākum declaratively; Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾisha, Muʿāwiya, Abū ʿImrān, and others lengthen it as a question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ألهاكم على الخبر وابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r4.speaker: أبو بكر وابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r4.claim: Another transmission uses two hamzas, making the question a rebuke and confirmation of the ugliness of their conduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p536/r4.anchor: وعن أبي بكر الصديق وابن عباس أيضا والشعبي وأبي العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي في رواية:

FARRA:v3p287/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p287/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p287/r1.claim: Two Quraysh clans, Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm, competed in counting the living and then the dead to prove which had more people.
FARRA:v3p287/r1.anchor: نزلت فى حيين من قريش تفاخروا: أيهم أكثر عددا؟ وهما: بنو عبد مناف وبنو سهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p538#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p538#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p538#2/r1.claim: Al-takāthur is competition in the number of people and kinship ties.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r1.claim: Al-lahw originally means heedlessness, then broadened to anything that occupies someone; customary usage narrows it to a pleasurable distraction near play, while here it makes people heedless.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r1.anchor: وأصل اللهو الغفلة ثم شاع في كل شاغل وخصه العرف بالشاغل الذي يسر المرء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r2.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r2.claim: Al-Raghib defines diversion as whatever distracts someone from what matters to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r2.anchor: وقال الراغب اللهو مايشغلك عما يعني ويهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#2/r3.claim: Al-takathur is competing and boasting over who has more, each group claiming numerical superiority.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r7.claim: The rivalry distracted people from the religious duty that truly matters; omitting the object of distraction magnifies the reproach through ambiguity and emphasizes the blame.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r7.anchor: والمعنى ألهاكم ذلك وهو لايعنيكم ولا يجدي عليكم في دنياكم وآخرتكم عما يعنيكم من أمر الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r8.claim: An alternative reading says wealth and children distracted people until death and burial; Ibn Abbas is cited for this interpretation, with al-Hasan also reported by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Abi Shayba.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ألهاكم التكاثر بالاموال والاولاد إلى أن متم وقبرتم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r17.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r17.claim: These readers lengthen the initial alif in alhakum, making the phrase interrogative.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r17.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة آلهاكم بالمد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r18.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وابن عباس والشعبي وأبي العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r18.claim: A transmission from these readers has two hamzas at the start, also forming an interrogative for confirmation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223#3/r18.anchor: وروى عن أبي بكر الصديق رضى الله عنه وابن عباس أيضا والشعبي وابي العالية وأبن أبي عبلة والكسائي في رواية أألهاكم بهمزتين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r1.claim: Al-takathur is rivalry and boasting in wealth and numbers that distracts people from obeying God and escaping His anger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r1.anchor: شغلتكم المباهاة والمفاخرة والمكاثرة بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة ربكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the passage concerns Jews boasting that they outnumbered one another; the rivalry distracted them until they died astray.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت في اليهود، قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان، وبنو فلان أكثر من بني فلان،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r4.claim: They say two Quraysh clans, Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm, competed over noblemen and numbers, then counted their dead in graves; Banu Sahm claimed more because they had been more numerous in pre-Islamic times.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في حيين من قريش؛ بني عبد مناف بن قصي، وبني سهم بن عمرو، كان بينهم تفاخر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r5.speaker: أبوه
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r5.claim: The father of Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah says the Prophet explained that a person owns only what he eats, wears, or gives as charity and sends ahead.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p515#2/r5.anchor: عن أبيه قال: انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ هذه الآية: "ألهاكم التكاثر"، قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.claim: ألهاكم means it distracted you into amusement, originally turning someone from attention; التكاثر is boasting about abundance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.anchor: { ألهكم } شغلكم وأصله الصرف إلى اللهو منقول من لها إذا غفل. { التكاثر } التباهي بالكثرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r3.claim: Alternatively, worldly competition in wealth and children distracts people until death and burial; visiting graves is a metaphor for dying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:102:1-2/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه { ألهكم التكاثر } بالأموال والأولاد إلى أن متم وقبرتم

BINTSHATI:v1p195/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r1.claim: The Meccan surah is commonly dated as the sixteenth in revelation, after al-Kawthar; its concise, emphatic warning dominates its tone.
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r1.anchor: السورة مكية بلا خلاف، وهي السادسة عشرة في ترتيب النزول، على المشهور

BINTSHATI:v1p195/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r2.speaker: النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r2.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī links this surah to al-Qāriʿah; the author rejects a chronological link because Takāthur precedes it by thirteen surahs, while allowing a shared warning tone in the muṣḥaf arrangement.
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r2.anchor: وقد ربطها بعض المفسرين - كالنيسابورى - بسورة القارعة

BINTSHATI:v1p195/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r3.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī treats the opening as a reproachful question rather than a declarative sentence.
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r3.anchor: لكن "الرازي" أخرجها من الإخبار إلى الاستفهام بمعنى التوبيخ والتقريع

BINTSHATI:v1p195/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r4.claim: The declarative reading warns more forcefully because it states that distraction by accumulation actually occurred, rather than asking whether it did.
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r4.anchor: والخبرية هنا أوقع في الزجر وأبلغ في الوعيد

BINTSHATI:v1p195/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r5.claim: Lahw means what distracts; its root may evoke the mill-hand’s handful that occupies the grinder and keeps it turning.
BINTSHATI:v1p195/r5.anchor: واللهو لغة، ما يلهى الإنسان. ولعل أصل استعماله في اللهوة

BINTSHATI:v1p196/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r1.claim: In al-Takāthur, the specific distraction is accumulation itself, from the root for abundance and increase.
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r1.anchor: أن الإلهاء فيها بالتكاثر. وهو لغة

BINTSHATI:v1p196/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses lahw for many kinds of futile distraction, including a person, money and children, trade, hopes, and speech.
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r2.anchor: أو أموال وأولاد: {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا

BINTSHATI:v1p196/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r3.claim: Qur’anic coordination of play and lahw shows that a distraction need not be playful.
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r3.anchor: وصنيع القرآن يؤذن بأن اللهو أيضاً قد يكون ليس بلعب

BINTSHATI:v1p196/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r4.claim: Takāthur derives from abundance and growth in quantity; abundance can figuratively suggest honor, unlike scarcity’s association with abasement.
BINTSHATI:v1p196/r4.anchor: وهو لغة: تفاعل من الكثرة نقيض القلة، ونماء العدد

BINTSHATI:v1p197/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī conflates mutual boasting and accumulation, but the author rejects redundancy because the Qur’an coordinates takāthur separately from tafākhur.
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r1.anchor: وجعل "الرازي" التفاخر والتكاثر شيئاً واحداً، وهو ما لا يوافق نسق آية الحديد

BINTSHATI:v1p197/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r2.claim: In al-Ḥadīd, takāthur means scrambling for worldly goods and seeking to monopolize them, a stage beyond frivolity, distraction, decoration, and boastful rivalry; al-Nīsābūrī also reports this view.
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r2.anchor: وإنه التكالب على حطام الدنيا ومحاولة الاستئثار به

BINTSHATI:v1p197/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r3.speaker: جمهرة المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r3.claim: Most exegetes understand takāthur as boasting and rivalry, influenced by reports about the occasion of revelation.
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r3.anchor: وإن يكن جمهرة المفسرين أكثر ميلاً إلى عد التكاثر هنا مباهاة وتفاخراً

BINTSHATI:v1p197/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r4.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the verse concerns boasting over wealth and numbers; Qatādah reports clans claiming to outnumber one another.
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r4.anchor: فالإمام الطبري ذهب إلى "أنها المباهاة بكثرة المال والعدد

BINTSHATI:v1p197/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r5.speaker: البحر المحيط
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r5.claim: Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ reports that the verse was revealed concerning the Jews.
BINTSHATI:v1p197/r5.anchor: وفي (البحر المحيط) أنها نزلت في اليهود

BINTSHATI:v1p198/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p198/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p198/r1.claim: Because the verse leaves the object of accumulation unspecified, the author rejects restricting it to money, numbers, or the dead, and also rejects limiting its scope to blameworthy kinds by importing a restriction.
BINTSHATI:v1p198/r1.anchor: ما ذهب الراغب، أو نقصره على العدد كما قال الرازي، أو الموتى كما في النيسابورى

BINTSHATI:v1p198/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p198/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p198/r2.claim: The address covers everyone distracted by accumulating worldly adornments such as wealth and children, whatever the specific reported occasion.
BINTSHATI:v1p198/r2.anchor: والخطاب هنا عام لكل من ألهاهم التكاثر والتكالب على زينة الدنيا من مال وولد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r1.claim: The surah identifies the cause of ruin at the gathering: competing to accumulate wealth and becoming attached to the passing world; its name signals this.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r1.anchor: الجمع للمال ، والإخلاد إلى دار الزوال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r2.claim: The basmala describes divine majesty, universal provision and guidance, and the completion of mercy for those whom God loves.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516/r2.anchor: الذي عم بالإنعام ، بالبيان - بعد الاتهام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r1.claim: The surah identifies the cause of ruin at the gathering: competing to accumulate wealth and becoming attached to the passing world; its name signals this.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r1.anchor: الجمع للمال ، والإخلاد إلى دار الزوال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r2.claim: The basmala describes divine majesty, universal provision and guidance, and the completion of mercy for those whom God loves.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#s102/r2.anchor: الذي عم بالإنعام ، بالبيان - بعد الاتهام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r1.claim: The surah opens after the description of the Hour and its doomed group by identifying the cause of misery and warning people away from it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r1.anchor: افتتح هذه بعلة الشقاوة ومبدأ الحشر لينزجر السامع عن هذا السبب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r2.claim: Takāthur is boasting in abundant, passing possessions such as wealth, status, and children; it diverts people from death, the afterlife, worship, and competing in good deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r2.anchor: المباهاة والمفاخرة بكثرة الأعراض الفانية من متاع الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r3.claim: Desire and love of ease make people heedless and their scales light; the object of distraction is left unstated to emphasize its importance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p516#2/r3.anchor: لأنكم لا تسلمون بما غلب عليكم من الجهل الذي سببه شهوة النفس وحب اراحة فخفت موازينكم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the warning to al-Qāriʿah: people are distracted from preparing for its horrors by competing in numbers, kin, and family.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تقدم ذكر القارعة وعظيم أهوالها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r2.claim: The phrase is a threat and rebuke; the repeated warning strengthens it, and the omitted result of 'if you knew with certain knowledge' is that accumulation would not distract you.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r2.anchor: وحذف جواب ( لو ) والتقدير : لو تعلمون علم اليقين لما شغلكم التكاثر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r5.claim: The ordered universe and pervasive human injustice imply a wise Creator who will resurrect people to judge them, as He has power to create them and has promised through revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r5.anchor: علم قطعا أنه يبعثه ليحكم بينهم لأنه كما قدر على إبدائهم يقدر على إعادتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r6.claim: Kallā is a forceful command to stop chasing useless worldly distinction: humans were created for a great purpose, not to compete for transient goods.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r6.anchor: أي ارتدعوا أتم ردع وانزجروا أعظم زجر عن الاشتغال بما لا يجدي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r7.claim: The author illustrates misplaced priorities with people who pursue more than daily needs and scholars who neglect essential Qur'an or law for anomalous opinions and trivial details.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p517/r7.anchor: من ترك المهم من التفسير واشتغل بالأقوال الشاذة أو ترك المهم من الفقه واشتغل بنوادر الفروغ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.claim: He says those earlier traits also produce obsession with accumulation, slander and mockery, and pride in the people of the Elephant.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.anchor: وانجر أثناء ذلك مما تثيره هذه الصفات الأولية ما ذكر فيها أيضا كالشغل بالتكاثر , والطعن على الناس ولمزهم

NAHHAS:v5p283/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p283/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p283/r1.claim: The best sense is that rivalry in abundance distracted people from obedience until burial; this verse indicates punishment in the grave.
NAHHAS:v5p283/r1.anchor: أصوب ما قيل في معناه أن المعنى ألهاكم التكاثر عن طاعة الله جل إلى أن صرتم إلى المقابر فدفنتم ودلت هذه الآية على عذاب القبر لا بعدها

NAHHAS:v5p283/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p283/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
NAHHAS:v5p283/r3.claim: A report from Zirr says the chapter was revealed about punishment in the grave and was recited through ‘No indeed, you will know.’
NAHHAS:v5p283/r3.anchor: نزل في عذاب القبر ألهاكم التكاثر

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and consists of eight verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r1.anchor: مكية وآياتها ثمان مقدمة السورة الآية 1 - 8

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Surat al-Takathur was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: نزلت بمكة سورة {ألهاكم التكاثر

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r3.claim: The Prophet says reciting al-Takathur answers the challenge of reciting a thousand verses in a day.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألا يستطيع أحدكم أن يقرأ ألف آية في كل يوم

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r4.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r4.claim: The Companions called the surah al-Mughira.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي هلال رضي الله عنه قال: كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسمون {ألهاكم التكاثر} المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r5.claim: Abdullah reports hearing the Prophet recite al-Takathur.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الشخير رضي الله عنه قال: انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r6.claim: A variant adds that wealth also includes what one gives away and sends ahead.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r6.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقول ابن آدم مالي مالي وهل لك من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r7.claim: The Prophet says a person’s wealth is food consumed, clothing worn out, and charity preserved; the rest is left to others.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقول العبد مالي مالي وإنما له من ماله ثلاثة ما أكل فأفنى

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r8.claim: A report through al-Hasan similarly limits a person’s wealth to what was eaten, worn, or given away.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقول ابن آدم مالي مالي وماله من ماله إلا ما أكل فأفنى

DURR-FULL:v8p609/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r9.claim: A weak report promises Paradise to whoever weeps when the surah is recited, or at least pretends to weep.
DURR-FULL:v8p609/r9.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إني قارئ عليكم سورة {ألهاكم التكاثر} فمن بكى فقد دخل الجنة

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r1.claim: The Prophet repeats the promise: whoever weeps at the second recitation enters Paradise; whoever cannot weep should feign it.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r1.anchor: فقال: إني قارئها عليكم الثانية فمن بكى فله الجنة ومن لم يقدر أن يبكي فليتباك

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says a saying about wishing for a third valley of wealth and death filling the belly had been treated as Qurʾan until this surah was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r2.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه قال: كنا نرى هذا من القرآن لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال لتمنى واديا ثالثا ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r3.claim: Qatada says people boasted that their clan outnumbered another until the contest distracted them and they died astray.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {ألهاكم التكاثر} قال: قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r4.claim: Qatada says the verse was revealed about the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ألهاكم التكاثر} قال: نزلت في اليهود

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r5.claim: Ali says the surah was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r5.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: نزلت {ألهاكم التكاثر} في عذاب القبر

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the rivalry is over wealth and children.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ألهاكم التكاثر} قال: في الأموال والأولاد

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r8.claim: The Prophet says he fears rivalry in accumulation more than poverty and deliberate wrongdoing more than mistakes.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما أخشى عليكم الفقر ولكن أخشى عليكم التكاثر وما أخشى عليكم الخطأ ولكن أخشى عليكم التعمد

DURR-FULL:v8p610/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r9.claim: The Prophet glosses rivalry as distraction from obedience and reaching the graves as the arrival of death.
DURR-FULL:v8p610/r9.anchor: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {ألهاكم التكاثر} يعني عن الطاعة {حتى زرتم المقابر} قال: يقول: حتى يأتيكم الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r1.claim: The Prophet glosses mutual rivalry as distracting people from obedience until death brings them to the graves.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r1.anchor: عن أبيه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : الهاكم التكاثر عن الطاعة ، حتى زرتم المقابر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r2.speaker: سعيد بن هلال
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Hilal says the Prophet's Companions called the sura al-Mughira.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن هلال رضي الله عنه قال : كان اصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسمون الهكم التكاثر المغيرة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r3.speaker: ابن بريدة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r3.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the sura was revealed about two Ansari clans who competed over the numbers of the living, then boasted over the dead in the graves.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r3.anchor: عن ابن بريدة في قوله : الهاكم التكاثر قال : نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الانصار

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r4.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r4.claim: Ali says they kept doubting the punishment of the grave until the phrase about visiting the graves was revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r4.anchor: عن علي قال : ما زلنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت الهاكم التكاثر : حتى زرتم المقابر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r5.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says a grave is only a visit, and a visitor must return to his home.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r5.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران قال : كنت جالسا عند عمر بن عبد العزيز فقرا الهاكم التكاثر . حتى زرتم المقابر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r6.claim: Qatadah says rival clans boasted that they had more people than others, and the rivalry distracted them until they died astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه الهاكم التكاثر قال : قالوا : نحن اكثر من بني فلان وبنو فلان اكثر من بني فلان

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r7.claim: Qatadah also says the verse was revealed about the Jews.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3459/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : الهاكم التكاثر قال : نزلت في اليهود

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3460/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3460/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3460/r1.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz repeats that the graves are a visit and a visitor must return home.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3460/r1.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز انه قرا : الهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر ثم قال : ما ارى المقابر الا زيارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r1.claim: Most codices and tafsirs, including al-Tirmidhi's heading, call it al-Takathur; some call it Alhakum, as al-Bukhari titles it, while companions reportedly called it al-Maqbara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r1.anchor: وسميت في معظم المصاحف ومعظم التفاسير ( سورة التكاثر ) وكذلك عنونها الترمذي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r2.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r2.claim: Said ibn Abi Hilal reports that the Prophet's companions called the surah al-Maqbara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن أبي هلال : كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسمونها ( المقبرة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil report a Meccan occasion involving a rivalry between Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm; al-Qurtubi attributes the account to them and Ibn Abbas.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل : أنها نزلت في مفاخرة جرت بين بني عبد مناف وبني سهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r4.claim: Al-Itqan prefers a Madinan setting, citing a report about two Ansari clans and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's statement that Muslims had recited a saying about Adam's wealth as Qur'an until this surah came.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r4.anchor: وفي ( الإتقان ) : المختار أنها مدنية . قال : ويدل له ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r5.claim: The Ubayy report does not prove a Madinan revelation: “we” could mean Muslims generally, who had mistaken a saying for Qur'an until the Prophet clarified it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r5.anchor: إذ يجوز أن يريد بضمير كنا } المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r6.claim: The warning's severe tone and content indicate a Meccan audience of polytheists, since the behavior described does not fit Muslims at that time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r6.anchor: والذي يظهر من معاني السورة وغلظة وعيدها أنها مكية وأن المخاطب بها فريق من المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r7.claim: The reported rivalry had Banu Abd Manaf count living nobles, then their dead; Banu Sahm surpassed them by three graves because their pre-Islamic numbers had been greater.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r7.anchor: ثم قالوا نعد موتانا حتى زاروا القبور فعدوا القبور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi and al-Baghawi transmit the rivalry account from Muqatil and al-Kalbi, with al-Qurtubi also citing them and Ibn Abbas.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p517/r8.anchor: وسبب نزولها فيما قاله الواحدي والبغوي عن مقاتل والكلبي والقرطبي عنهما وعن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r1.speaker: أبو بريدة الجرمي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r1.claim: Abu Burayda al-Jurmi reports that Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith of the Ansar boasted of living people, then pointed to notable graves in each group; the verse was revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي بريدة الجرمي قال : نزلت في قبيلين من الأنصار بني حارثة وبني الحارث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r2.claim: On the Meccan chronology, it is the sixteenth surah revealed, after al-Kawthar and before al-Maʿun, and has eight verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r2.anchor: وقد عدت السادسة عشرة في ترتيب نزول السور ، نزلت بعد سورة الكوثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r3.claim: The surah rebukes neglect of Qur'anic evidence and Islam's call in favor of wealth, accumulation, and ancestral boasting until death, and warns against that course.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p518/r3.anchor: اشتملت على التوبيخ على اللهو عن النظر في دلائل القرآن ودعوة الإسلام بإيثار المال والتكاثر به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r1.claim: Alhakum means that something occupied people and diverted them from what they ought to attend to; takathur is competitive accumulation of desired things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r1.anchor: { ألهاكم } أي شغلكم عما يجب عليكم الاشتغال به لأن اللهو شغل يصرف عن تحصيل أمر مهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r2.claim: The competition can concern wealth or numbers of children and allies used for prestige, as in the boast about having more wealth and children.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r2.anchor: فمنه تكاثر في الأموال ، ومنه تكاثر في العدد من الأولاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r3.claim: The author connects the numbers boast with the statement that people claimed greater wealth and children and therefore no punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r3.anchor: قال تعالى : { وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين } ( سبأ : 35 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r4.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r4.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line says he is not the one with the most counted heads, but honor belongs to the larger group, illustrating rivalry in numbers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r4.anchor: وقال الأعشى : ولست بالأكثر منهم حصى وإنما العزة للكاثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r5.claim: Muslim reports that Ibn al-Shikhkhir heard the Prophet recite the verse and explain that a person keeps saying “my wealth,” though only what he consumes, wears out, or gives away remains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r5.anchor: روى مسلم عن عبد الله بن الشخير قال : ( انتهيت إلى رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r6.claim: The hadith illustrates one sense of accumulation, selected to suit the occasion of that admonition, and is compatible with the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r6.anchor: فهذا جار مجرى التفسير لمعنى من معاني التكاثر اقتضاه حال الموعظة ساعتئذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r7.claim: The severe threats identify the addressees as polytheists, since this behavior was not a Muslim custom then; wealthy chiefs are especially targeted for preferring comfort to the Prophet's call and suppressing it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r7.anchor: والخطاب للمشركين بقرينة غلظة الوعيد بقوله : { كلا سوف تعلمون ثم كلا سوف تعلمون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r8.claim: Although directly addressed to polytheists, the warning teaches Muslims to resist love of wealth when it distracts from good and to fear death arriving during heedlessness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p519/r8.anchor: فيعلمون أنهم محذرون من التلبس بشيء من ذلك فيحذرون من أن يلهيهم حب المال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p520/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p520/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p520/r4.claim: Alternatively, the endpoint is the object of rivalry: they compete over everything, even graves, as in the report about Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm counting tombs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p520/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الغاية للمتكاثر به الدال عليه التكاثر ، أي بكل شيء حتى بالقبور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r1.claim: Alha means to distract through pleasures, as in idle talk, sounds, and preoccupation with women; the verse rebukes and grieves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r1.anchor: «ألهى» معناه: شغل بلذاته، ومنه لهو الحديث والأصوات واللهو بالنساء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعمران الجوني وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Imran al-Jawni, and Abu Salih read the opening as a question.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعمران الجوني وأبو صالح: «أألهاكم» على الاستفهام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r3.claim: Takathur means boasting competitively about wealth, children, and numbers, a worldly habit escaped only by learned, pious people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r3.anchor: والتكاثر هي المفاخرة بالأموال والأولاد والعدد جملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r4.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r4.claim: Al-Aʿsha's poem contrasts not having the largest pebble count with the glory of being numerous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r4.anchor:
وقد قال الأعشى: [السريع]
ولست بالأكثر منهم حصى ... وإنما العزة للكاثر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r5.claim: The Prophet says a person's true possessions are only what he ate, wore, or gave away in charity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p518#3/r5.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يقول ابن آدم مالي مالي، وهل لك من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r1.claim: Love of worldly life, its pleasures, and its adornments distracts people from seeking the afterlife until death brings them to the graves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r1.anchor: شغلكم حب الدنيا ونعيمها وزهرتها عن طلب الآخرة وابتغائها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r2.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says rivalry distracted people from obedience until death came; Ibn Kathīr gives no grading here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says the rivalry concerns wealth and children.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: {ألهاكم التكاثر} في الأموال والأولاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says they used to regard the saying that a son of Adam could have a valley of gold as Qurʾān until this sūra was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، عن أبي بن كعب قال: كنا نرى هذا من القرآن حتى نزلت: {ألهاكم التكاثر}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says a person claims “my wealth,” but owns only what they eat and consume, wear and wear out, or give in charity and send ahead.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r5.anchor: عن أبيه قال: انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقول: " {ألهاكم التكاثر} يقول ابن آدم: مالي مالي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r6.claim: A report in Muslim says a person's usable wealth is food consumed, clothing worn out, and charity retained as reward; the rest is left behind.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r6.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يقول العبد: مالي مالي؟ وإنما له من ماله ثلاث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r7.claim: The dead person is followed by family, wealth, and deeds; family and wealth return, while deeds remain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p472#2/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يتبع الميت ثلاثة، فيرجع اثنان ويبقى معه واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r1.claim: The Prophet says that old age leaves a son of Adam with two persistent traits: greed and hope; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r1.anchor: عن أنس: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يهرم ابن آدم وتبقى منه اثنتان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r2.speaker: الأحنف بن قيس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r2.claim: Al-Aḥnaf tells a man that a coin is truly his only when he spends it seeking reward or gratitude.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r2.anchor: فقال: إنما هو لك إذا أنفقته في أجر أو ابتغاء شكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r3.speaker: الأحنف بن قيس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r3.claim: Al-Aḥnaf cites a poet: money held back belongs to you only in custody, while money spent is truly yours.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r3.anchor: أنت للمال إذا أمسكته … فإذا أنفقته فالمال لك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r4.speaker: ابن بريدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r4.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the sūra was revealed about Banū Ḥāritha and Banū al-Ḥārith boasting over living and dead members of their tribes at the graves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r4.anchor: عن ابن بريدة في قوله: {ألهاكم التكاثر} قال: نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r5.claim: Qatāda says people boasted that their tribe was more numerous than another, while their members kept dying until all became grave-dwellers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: {ألهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر} كانوا يقولون نحن أكثر من بني فلان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r7.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r7.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Muslims continued to doubt punishment in the grave until this sūra was revealed; Ibn Kathīr later cites al-Tirmidhī calling the report gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p473/r7.anchor: عن علي قال: ما زلنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت: {ألهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر}

JISHUMI:v10p7523/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r1.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r1.claim: He says Sūrat al-Takāthur is Medinan; Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda say it is Meccan.
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: مدنية، وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: مكية

JISHUMI:v10p7523/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r2.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet promises that the reciter will not be called to account for worldly blessings and will receive a reward like reciting a thousand verses.
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r2.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي صلى الله عليه: من قرأ (ألهاكم التكاثر) لم يحاسبه الله بالنعم

JISHUMI:v10p7523/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r3.claim: After the preceding chapter warned that disbelievers' destination is Hell, this chapter explains what led them there.
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r3.anchor: ولما ختم السورة بوعيد الكفار، وأن أمهم هاوية، افتتح هذه السورة ببيان ما أدى بهم إلى ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7523/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r5.claim: Ilhāʾ means turning someone from serious matters toward diversion; the verb is attributed to takāthur because boasting about abundance causes distraction.
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r5.anchor: وحقيقة قوله: (ألهاكم التكاثر) أي: لهيتم بالتكاثر، فأضاف الفعل إلى التكاثر اتساعا

JISHUMI:v10p7523/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r6.claim: Takāthur is competitive boasting in the abundance of distinctions; the tafaʿala pattern can mark reciprocity, forced pretense, or acquiring a quality.
JISHUMI:v10p7523/r6.anchor: والتكاثر: التفاخر بكثرة المناقب، تكاثر القوم تكاثرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r1.claim: ألهاه and أقهاه mean that something occupied or distracted a person; التكاثر is rivalry and boasting in numbers, each group claiming superiority.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r1.anchor: ألهاه عن كذا وأقهاه : إذا شغله . و { التكاثر } التباري في الكثرة والتباهي بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r2.claim: Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm competed in headcounts; after the former initially outnumbered them, Banu Sahm counted the living and dead and prevailed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r2.anchor: روي أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا أيهم أكثر عددا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r3.claim: The rivalry continued from counting the living to counting the dead in graves, a mocking description of their competition beyond death; some say they literally visited graves to count and name their dead.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r3.anchor: عبر عن بلوغهم ذكر الموتى بزيارة المقابر تهكما بهم . وقيل : كانوا يزورون المقابر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r4.claim: The rivalry may instead be in wealth and children, distracting people until they die and are buried, after spending life pursuing the world instead of religion and the afterlife; visiting graves is a euphemism for death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r4.anchor: منفقين أعماركم في طلب الدنيا والاستباق إليها والتهالك عليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r5.claim: Two poetic examples use visiting graves as a figure for dying, including one in which Abu Malik visits graves and becomes the vilest of their visitors.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798/r5.anchor: زار القبور أبو مالك … فأصبح ألأم زوارها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the opening as a rhetorical question seeking affirmation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p798#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : ( أألهاكم ) ؟ على الاستفهام الذي معناه التقرير

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r1.claim: Alhakum means it occupied you or made you forget, distracting you from obeying God and worshipping the Creator.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r1.anchor: في { ألهاكم } وجهان : أحدهما : شغلكم . الثاني : أنساكم , ومعناه ألهاكم عن طاعة ربكم وشغلكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the rivalry is competing in wealth and children.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r2.anchor: أحدها : التكاثر بالمال والأولاد , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r3.claim: Qatada says it is boasting about clans and tribes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r3.anchor: الثاني : التفاخر بالعشائر والقبائل , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r4.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says it is preoccupation with livelihood and trade.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p330/r4.anchor: الثالث : التشاغل بالمعاش والتجارة , قاله الضحاك .

MUQATIL:102:1-7/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r1.claim: Two Quraysh clans, Banu ʿAbd Manāf and Banu Sahm, disputed and boasted by comparing their leaders, honor, protection, and numbers.
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r1.anchor: وذلك أن حيين من قريش من بني عبد مناف بن قصى، وبنى سهم بن عمرو بن مرة بن كعب، كان بينهم لحاء فافتخروا

MUQATIL:102:1-7/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r2.claim: They settled the rivalry by counting graves; Banu Sahm surpassed Banu ʿAbd Manāf by three houses, having been more numerous in pre-Islamic times.
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r2.anchor: فكاثرهم بنو سهم بثلاثة أبيات، لأنهم كانوا أكثر عددا في الجاهلية من بني عبد مناف

MUQATIL:102:1-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r3.claim: The rivalry of multiplying and boasting distracted them from remembering the afterlife.
MUQATIL:102:1-7/r3.anchor: فأنزل الله في الحيين { ألهاكم التكاثر } يقول: شغلكم التكاثر عن ذكر الآخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#12/r1.claim: Rivalry and striving to outdo one another in accumulating wealth and children distracts people from obeying God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#12/r1.anchor: سغلكم التبارى فى الكثرة والتناهى بها فى الأموال والأولاد عن طاعة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.claim: Alhaka means occupied or distracted; rivalry in wealth and numbers diverts people from obedience until death and burial.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r1.anchor: أي شغلكم المباهاة بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة الله، حتى متم ودفنتم في المقابر.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r2.claim: A poem uses alhaytu to mean I distracted or occupied her.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r3.claim: Another gloss takes alhaka as made you forget; takathur can mean rivalry in possessions and children, as Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r4.claim: Qatada says the rivalry is boasting about tribes and clans.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: أي التفاخر بالقبائل والعشائر.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the distraction is being preoccupied with livelihood and trade.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أي ألهاكم التشاغل بالمعاش والتجارة.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r6.claim: The root l-h-y means to forget, stop mentioning, or turn away from something; alha means occupied, and lahha means entertained or diverted.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r6.anchor: يقال: لهيت عن كذا بالكسر ألهى لهيا ولهيانا: إذا سلوت عنه، وتركت ذكره، وأضربت عنه. وألهاه: أي شغله.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r7.speaker: مقاتل وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r7.claim: Some say it descended about Jews boasting that their lineages outnumbered one another until they died in error.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل وقتادة وغيرهما: نزلت في اليهود حين قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان،

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says the surah descended about a clan of the Ansar.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: نزلت في فخذ من الأنصار.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r11.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r11.claim: Amr ibn Dinar swore that the surah descended about merchants.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r11.anchor: وعن عمرو بن دينار: حلف أن هذه السورة نزلت في التجار.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r12.speaker: شبيان عن قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r12.claim: Shayban transmits from Qatada that it descended concerning the People of the Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r12.anchor: وعن شبيان عن قتادة قال: نزلت في أهل الكتاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r14.speaker: مطرف عن أبيه
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r14.claim: In Muslim, Mutarrif's father hears the Prophet explain that the only wealth a person truly keeps is what he consumes, wears out, or gives away; the rest is left behind.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2/r14.anchor: عن مطرف عن أبيه قال: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ { ألهاكم التكاثر } قال: «يقول ابن آدم: مالي مالي! وهل لك يا ابن آدم من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت،

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r1.claim: Continuing the report introduced in the preceding segment, the Prophet says that a person would desire two valleys of gold and only dust fills his mouth, while God accepts repentance.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r1.anchor: لو أن لابن آدم واديا من ذهب، لأحب أن يكون له واديان، ولن يملأ فاه إلا التراب،

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r2.speaker: ثابت عن أنس عن أبي
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r2.claim: Thabit transmits that the Companions once regarded this saying as Qur'an until al-Takathur was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r2.anchor: قال ثابت عن أنس عن أبي: كنا نرى هذا من القرآن، حتى نزلت { ألهاكم التكاثر }.

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi calls that an authentic, explicit report whose interpretive significance commentators overlooked.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهذا نص صحيح مليح، غاب عن أهل التفسير فجهلوا وجهلوا،

QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet defined wealth rivalry as gathering money unlawfully, withholding its due, and hoarding it in containers.
QURTUBI-FULL:102:1-2#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: " قرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { ألهاكم التكاثر } قال: «تكاثر الأموال: جمعها من غير حقها،

QUTB-ZILAL:102:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:102:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:102:1/r1.claim: The Meccan surah sounds like a grave warning calling to heedless, intoxicated people who compete in wealth, children, and worldly honors while nearing death, deceived about what follows.
QUTB-ZILAL:102:1/r1.anchor: أيها السادرون المخمورون . أيها اللاهون المتكاثرون بالأموال والأولاد وأعراض الحياة

ZAJJAJ:v5p357/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p357/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p357/r1.claim: Competition for money and children distracted people from obeying God.
ZAJJAJ:v5p357/r1.anchor: أي شغلكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد عن طاعة الله

RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r1.claim: Ilhāʾ is turning someone toward diversion; diversion follows desire and entails neglecting something else, so ألهاني means distracted or made me forget.
RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r1.anchor: الإلهاء الصرف إلى اللهو . واللهو الانصراف

RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r2.claim: Takāthur means boasting competitively about wealth, status, and distinctions; Abu Muslim says its morphology can express mutual competition, effort to increase, or simply becoming numerous.
RAZI-FULL:v32p72/r2.anchor: والتكاثر التباهي بكثرة المال والجاه والمناقب

RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r2.claim: The verse condemns competition in every worldly pleasure, including numbers, wealth, status, relatives, supporters, and armies.
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r2.anchor: ويدخل فيه التكاثر بالعدد وبالمال والجاه والأقرباء والأنصار والجيش

RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r3.claim: ألهاكم can be a statement about the people's distraction or a reproachful question asking whether competition distracted them.
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r3.anchor: قوله : { ألهاكم } يحتمل أن يكون إخبارا عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r4.claim: Competition is not always blameworthy: the verse about pilgrimage water and the Kaaba key reports rivals boasting over religious services before ʿAli's claim of fighting unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك ما روى من تفاخر العباس بأن السقاية بيده

RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r5.claim: A person may display obedience and good character when it could encourage others; therefore competition in knowledge, devotion, and virtue is praiseworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r5.anchor: أنه يجوز للإنسان أن يفتخر بطاعاته ومحاسن أخلاقه إذا كان يظن أن غيره يقتدي به

RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r6.claim: The definite article in التكاثر refers to familiar worldly accumulation, not every kind of striving; that distraction obstructs worship, while competition in virtue is good.
RAZI-FULL:v32p73/r6.anchor: فالألف واللام في التكاثر ليسا للاستغراق ، بل للمعهود السابق

RAZI-FULL:v32p73#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p73#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p73#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the rivalry about wealth; a report from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir's father says a person's wealth is only what he consumed, wore, or gave away.
RAZI-FULL:v32p73#2/r4.anchor: استدلوا عليه بما روى مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير عن أبيه

STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r1.claim: Most consider al-Takāthur Makkan and place it after al-Kawthar; a minority call it Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r1.anchor: al-Takāthur is a Makkan sūrah, believed to follow Sūrah 108

STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r2.speaker: some Companions
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r2.claim: Some Companions reportedly called this “The Sūrah of the Grave.”
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r2.anchor: was reportedly called “The Sūrah of the Grave” by some Companions of the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r3.claim: The best-attested occasion concerns Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm boasting about numbers, counting the living then dead; Sahm prevailed because it had more pre-Islamic dead.
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r3.anchor: this sūrah was revealed about two clans of the Quraysh

STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r4.claim: Others say the verses address the People of the Book, specifically the Jews of Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r4.anchor: Others say that these verses are a reference to the People of the Book or specifically to the Jews of Madinah

STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r5.claim: The first two verses expose delusion in accumulating worldly goods, a theme elsewhere in the Qur'an; vv. 3–8 warn persistent accumulators they will know Hellfire with certainty.
STUDYQURAN:102:intro/r5.anchor: The first two verses speak of the delusion of accumulating worldly goods, which is referenced throughout the Quran

STUDYQURAN:102:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r1.claim: Competing for worldly gains distracts people from obeying God and remembering the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r1.anchor: Vying for increase in worldly gains distracts people from obedience to God and remembering the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:102:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r2.claim: Lahw, “distraction,” is amusement that keeps people from reaching their real goals.
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r2.anchor: indicates an amusement, something that keeps people from achieving their real goals

STUDYQURAN:102:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r3.claim: The Qur'an warns against worldly life deluding people.
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r3.anchor: In this vein, the Quran advises, Let not the life of this world delude you

STUDYQURAN:102:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r4.claim: Takāthur means competing and boasting over anything sought for ego gratification rather than God's sake.
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r4.anchor: Vying for increase translates takāthur, which implies both competing and boasting. It can pertain to anything that people seek for the gratification of their egos

STUDYQURAN:102:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r5.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet defines takāthur as unjustly gathering wealth, withholding what is due, and hoarding it.
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r5.anchor: According to a saying attributed to the Prophet, it means gathering wealth without right, withholding it from those to whom it rightfully belongs, and hoarding it

STUDYQURAN:102:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r6.claim: When a Companion found the Prophet reciting the verse, he said wealth benefits a person only as food eaten, clothes worn, or charity spent.
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r6.anchor: the Prophet said, “The son of Adam says, ‘My wealth! My wealth!’ But do you get anything from your wealth except what you have eaten and finished

STUDYQURAN:102:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r7.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r7.claim: Another hadith says that if Adam's son had a valley of gold, he would want a second valley.
STUDYQURAN:102:1/r7.anchor: Another ḥadīth states, “If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would wish for it to be two valleys”

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.claim: Read after Sūrah 102, ʿaṣr can mean time generally: vying for increase wastes it, and time's blessing is what people will be questioned about.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.anchor: When viewed in relation to the previous sūrah, ʿaṣr can be understood as a reference to time in general, meaning that vying for increase (102:1) prevents people from spending their time

TAB:102:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:1/r1.speaker: author
TAB:102:1/r1.claim: Competition in boasting about abundant wealth and numbers distracts people from obeying God and avoiding His anger.
TAB:102:1/r1.anchor: ألهاكم أيها الناس المباهاة بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة ربكم ،   وعما ينجيكم من سخطه عليكم

TAB:102:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:1/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:102:1/r2.claim: Qatāda says tribes boasted that they outnumbered others until every one of them had died and entered the graves.
TAB:102:1/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {  ألهَاكُمُ التّكاثُرُ حتى زُرْتُمُ المَقابِرَ } قال :  كانوا يقولون :  نحن أكثر من بني فلان ،   ونحن أعدّ من بني فلان

TAB:102:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:1/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:102:1/r3.claim: The Prophet tells a reader that a person keeps only food consumed, clothes worn out, and charity sent ahead; this points to wealth as the object of competition.
TAB:102:1/r3.anchor: عن أبيه أنه انتهى إلى النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   وهو يقرأ :  {  ألهَاكُمُ التّكاثُرُ حَتّى زُرْتُمُ المَقابرَ } قال :  «ابنَ آدم ،   ليس لك من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت

TAB:102:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:1/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB:102:1/r4.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb says people thought a warning about endless desire for wealth was Qur'an until this surah was revealed, ending that uncertainty.
TAB:102:1/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك ،   عن أُبيّ بن كعب ،   قال :  كنا نرى أن هذا الحديث من القرآن :  «لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مالٍ ،   لتمنى واديا ثالثا

TAB:102:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:102:1/r5.speaker: author
TAB:102:1/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the Prophet's words after reciting the verse as evidence that التكاثر means competing in wealth.
TAB:102:1/r5.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعَقِب قراءته :  «ألهاكُمُ » :  ليس لك من مالك إلا كذا وكذا ،   ينبىء أن معنى ذلك عنده :  ألهاكم التكاثر :  المال

ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r1.claim: This early Meccan surah is a powerful prophetic passage about humanity's unbounded greed.
ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r1.anchor: THIS early Meccan surah is one of the most powerful, prophetic passages of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r2.claim: It especially addresses greed-driven tendencies that have come to dominate technological societies.
ASAD-NOTES:102:intro/r2.anchor: the tendencies which have come to dominate all human societies in our technological age

ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r1.claim: An exclusive pursuit of these gains blocks spiritual insight and acceptance of limits grounded in moral values.
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r1.anchor: A passionate pursuit of such endeavours, to the exclusion of everything else, bars man from all spiritual insight

ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r2.claim: The pursuit gradually destabilizes individuals and whole societies, eliminating their chance of happiness.
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r2.anchor: with the result that not only individuals but whole societies gradually lose all inner stability and, thus, all chance of happiness.

ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r3.claim: Unrestrained economic growth destroys the natural environment and brings frustration, unhappiness, and confusion to people losing their remaining spiritual orientation.
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r3.anchor: fundamentally wrong mode of life: an allusion to the gradual destruction of man's natural environment

ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r4.claim: The unchecked pursuit of economic growth has brought frustration and confusion and threatens the remnants of spiritual and religious orientation.
ASAD-NOTES:102:1/r4.anchor: an overriding, unrestrained pursuit of "economic growth" is bound to bring - and has, indeed, brought in our time - upon a mankind that is about to lose the remnants of all spiritual religious orientation

TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r1.claim: People are distracted from obeying their Lord and seeking deliverance from His anger by competing and boasting about abundance of wealth and numbers.
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r1.anchor: عن مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير، عن أبيه، أنه انتهى إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو يقرأ: {ألهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر} [التكاثر: 2] قال: «ابن آدم، ليس لك من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت

TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r2.claim: Qatadah describes tribes boasting that they outnumber other tribes until every generation falls away and all become people of the graves; this rivalry distracted them until they died astray.
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {ألهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر} [التكاثر: 2] قال: " كانوا يقولون: نحن أكثر من بني فلان، ونحن أعد من بني فلان، وهم كل يوم يتساقطون إلى آخرهم

TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r3.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r3.claim: After reciting the verse, the Prophet says a person's wealth is only what he consumes, wears out, or gives in charity and sends ahead.
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، أنه انتهى إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو يقرأ: {ألهاكم التكاثر حتى زرتم المقابر} [التكاثر: 2] قال: «ابن آدم، ليس لك من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت

TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says they had considered the saying about wanting a third valley of wealth and a belly filled only by earth to be Quran until this surah was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: كنا نرى أن هذا الحديث من القرآن: «لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال، لتمنى واديا ثالثا

TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r5.claim: The Prophet's comment after reciting the surah confirms that the abundance distracting people is wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p598#2/r5.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعقب قراءته: ألهاكم ليس لك من مالك إلا كذا وكذا، ينبئ أن معنى ذلك عنده: ألهاكم التكاثر: المال

TAB-FULL:v24p600/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p600/r2.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p600/r2.claim: Ali says they had doubted punishment in the grave until the surah was revealed through ‘you will know.’
TAB-FULL:v24p600/r2.anchor: عن زر، عن علي، قال: " كنا نشك في عذاب القبر، حتى نزلت هذه الآية: {ألهاكم التكاثر} [التكاثر: 1] إلى: {كلا سوف تعلمون} [التكاثر: 3] في عذاب القبر "

CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r1.claim: Paret glosses takāṯur as the urge to have more; Künstlinger proposes it is an Arabic rendering of Greek pleonexia, with the Greek comparative expressed by Arabic form VI.
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Sehr wahrscheinlich handelt es sich aber um eine Arabisierung von griech. pleonexia

CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r2.claim: If the Greek connection is right, the Quranic term likely reflects the Greek New Testament, whose examples include Luke's warning against greed; the Peshitta uses less similar words.
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Falls der von Künstlinger hergestellte Zusammenhang zutrifft, so dürfte im Hintergrund des koranischen Begriffs der griechische Originaltext des Neuen Testaments stehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Andrae
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r3.claim: Andrae compares the verse with Ephrem's picture of the worldly person as someone who always desires more.
CORPUSCORANICUM:102:1:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Andrae verweist im Zusammenhang mit dem vorliegenden Vers auf Ephrems Beschreibung des Weltmenschen als jemandem, der stets „mehr begehrt“

TABATABAI:102:1-6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r1.speaker: author
