TABATABAI:102:1-6/r1.claim: The surah sharply rebukes people distracted by competing over wealth, children, and numbers, warning of loss and punishment and that they will be questioned about blessings they met with ingratitude.
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r1.anchor: بيان توبيخ شديد للناس على تلهيهم بالتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد

TABATABAI:102:1-6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r2.claim: Raghib defines diversion as whatever occupies a person from what matters, and takathur as competing to have more wealth and prestige.
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r2.anchor: اللهو ما يشغل الإنسان عما يعنيه ويهمه. قال، ويقال ألهاه كذا أي شغله عما هو أهم إليه

TABATABAI:102:1-6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r4.claim: The contextual meaning is that competition for worldly goods and adornment distracts from remembering God until death, leaving people heedless throughout life.
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r4.anchor: شغلكم التكاثر في متاع الدنيا وزينتها والتسابق في تكثير العدة والعدة عما يهمكم

TABATABAI:102:1-6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r5.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r5.claim: Another interpretation has people boast about having more living men, then count and boast about their dead after all the living have died.
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r5.anchor: وقيل المعنى شغلكم التباهي والتباري بكثرة الرجال بأن يقول هؤلاء نحن أكثر رجالا

TABATABAI:102:1-6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r6.claim: The men-counting interpretation rests on reports that two Anṣar tribes first competed over the living and then the dead, or that Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm did so in Mecca, prompting the surah.
TABATABAI:102:1-6/r6.anchor: وهذا المعنى مبني على ما ورد في أسباب النزول أن قبيلتين من الأنصار تفاخرتا بالأحياء ثم بالأموات

TABATABAI:102:1-8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:102:1-8/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABATABAI:102:1-8/r3.claim: A report says the surah concerned Jews boasting that their group outnumbered others; the rivalry kept them deluded until death.
TABATABAI:102:1-8/r3.anchor: ألهاهم ذلك حتى ماتوا ضلالا عن قتادة

TABRISI:102:1-8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:102:1-8/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:102:1-8/r3.claim: Ilhāʾ means diverting someone toward pastime, while pastime is turning toward what desire invites.
TABRISI:102:1-8/r3.anchor: الإلهاء الصرف إلى اللهو واللهو الانصراف إلى ما يدعو إليه الهوى

TABRISI:102:1-8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:102:1-8/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:102:1-8/r4.claim: Takāthur is boasting about having more merits; ziyārah is visiting a place without settling there, also the root of deceptive imitation.
TABRISI:102:1-8/r4.anchor: والتكاثر التفاخر بكثرة المناقب يقال تكاثر القوم إذا تعادوا ما لهم من المناقب

TABRISI:102:1-7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:102:1-7/r1.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:102:1-7/r1.claim: The surah is said to address Jews who competed in numbers among their clans and died in error while distracted by rivalry.
TABRISI:102:1-7/r1.anchor: نزلت السورة في اليهود قالوا نحن أكثر من بني فلان وبنو فلان أكثر

TABRISI:102:1-7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:102:1-7/r2.speaker: أبو بريدة
TABRISI:102:1-7/r2.claim: Another report says the surah was revealed about an Ansari clan competing in numbers.
TABRISI:102:1-7/r2.anchor: نزلت في فخذ من الأنصار تفاخروا عن أبي بريدة

TABRISI:102:1-7/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:102:1-7/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:102:1-7/r4.claim: Rivalry in wealth and children distracted people from obedience to God and remembrance of the afterlife.
TABRISI:102:1-7/r4.anchor: أي شغلكم عن طاعة الله وعن ذكر الآخرة التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد

THALABI:v10p276#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p276#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p276#3/r1.claim: Rivalry in boasting about wealth and numbers distracts people from obeying God and escaping His anger.
THALABI:v10p276#3/r1.anchor: شغلتكم المباهاة والمفاخرة بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة ربكم

THALABI:v10p276#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p276#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p276#3/r3.claim: He says the surah came down about Jews comparing which clan was larger, a contest that distracted them until they died astray.
THALABI:v10p276#3/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت في اليهود قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان

THALABI:v10p276#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p276#3/r4.speaker: ابن بريدة
THALABI:v10p276#3/r4.claim: He says it came down about a clan among the Ansar who boasted against one another.
THALABI:v10p276#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن بريدة: نزلت في فخذ من الأنصار تفاخروا

THALABI:v10p276#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p276#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v10p276#3/r5.claim: They say two Quraysh clans disputed which had more leaders and numbers, then counted their dead in graves; Banu Sahm outnumbered Banu Abd Manaf by three households, prompting the revelation.
THALABI:v10p276#3/r5.anchor: مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في حيين من قريش: بني عبد مناف وبني قصي

THALABI:v10p276#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p276#3/r6.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p276#3/r6.claim: The Prophet says a person’s real possessions are only what he eats and consumes, wears and wears out, or gives in charity and sends ahead.
THALABI:v10p276#3/r6.anchor: عن أبيه قال: انتهيت إلى رسول الله (عليه السلام) وهو يقرأ هذه الآية: ألهاكم التكاثر قال: يقول ابن آدم: ما لي ما لي،

THALABI:v10p281/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p281/r4.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p281/r4.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s report, takathur is wrongful accumulation and withholding; the passage follows people through graves and judgment, then names five blessings: full stomach, cold drink, sleep, shade, and sound constitution.
THALABI:v10p281/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألهاكم التكاثر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r1.claim: Alha means to make someone forget or occupy him; lahiytu means to leave or turn away from something.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r1.anchor: ألهاني فلان عن كذا، أي أنساني، وشغلني، ولهيت عنه ألهى لهيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r2.claim: A report says Ibn al-Zubayr would leave his conversation when he heard thunder.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r2.anchor: أن ابن الزبير كان إذا سمع صوت الرعد لهي من حديثه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r3.claim: Al-takathur is boasting about wealth and numbers and competing over the abundance of one's merits.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p275#2/r3.anchor: والتكاثر: التباهي بكثرة المال والعدد، والتفاخر بكثرة المناقب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p276#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p276#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p276#2/r3.claim: The warning includes everyone who lets boasting and rivalry distract from obedience until death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p276#2/r3.anchor: ثم يدخل في هذا كل من اشتغل بالتكاثر والتفاخر عن طاعة الله حتى يأتيه الموت وهو على ذلك

WAHIDI-QT:102:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:102:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:102:1/r1.claim: Competing in wealth, children, and numbers distracts people from obedience to God.
WAHIDI-QT:102:1/r1.anchor: شغلكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد والعدد عن طاعة الله تعالى

WAHIDI-QT:102:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:102:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:102:2/r1.claim: Competing in wealth, children, and numbers distracts people from obedience to God.
WAHIDI-QT:102:2/r1.anchor: شغلكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد والعدد عن طاعة الله تعالى

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r1.claim: Ilhā derives from lahw, whose root sense is heedlessness; it means idly occupying and diverting people from their work and duty.

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r2.claim: Takāthur is rivalry and pride in having more, a delusive worldly contest in numbers or abundance.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r2.anchor: “Tekâsür” Çokluk kurumu, gururu, iddiası. Kesretten tefâ‘ul.

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r3.claim: The verse leaves both the object of distraction and the kind of abundance unstated, giving the wording comprehensive rhetorical scope; context still supplies qualifications.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r3.anchor: Neyin çokluğu ve neden alıkoyduğu zâhiren tasrih olunmayarak “ilhâ” ve “tekâsür” mutlak zikredilmiştir.

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r4.claim: In context, distraction means neglecting duties and useful remembrance, knowledge, reflection, gratitude, worship, and obedience; takathur means worldly abundance useless at the Scale and leaving only loss and punishment.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r4.anchor: Bundan evvelki sûrede “kāri‘a” ve “mîzan” zikredilmiş bulunduğu gibi, bundan sonra da kabirler zikrolunacağı cihetle

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r5.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the takathur in this context as competition in wealth and children.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r5.anchor: Buhârî’de İbn Abbas’tan “mal ve evlâdda tekâsür” denilmiştir.

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r6.claim: The definite article on takathur points to a known occasion of revelation, with reports describing tribal boasts over which group had more people.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r6.anchor: ٱلتَّكَاثُرُ’de ال ahd için olarak sebeb-i nüzûldeki mânaya işaret olur.

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r7.claim: Many exegetes report that Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm rivaled over their numbers, then counted or invoked their dead; the surah was revealed in response.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r7.anchor: Benî Abdi Menaf ile Benî Sehm, “hangimiz daha çoğuz” diye tefâhur edişmişlerdi

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r8.speaker: Ebû Büreyde
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r8.claim: Abu Burayda reports that the Ansari clans Banu Harith and Banu Hars listed their living notables, then went to the graves and compared their dead before the verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r8.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim’in Ebû Büreyde’den bir tahrîcine göre de; ensar kabilelerinden

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r9.claim: The reports both describe boasting by numerical comparison with the dead, but only the second has the rivals physically visit graves; it also suggests a Medinan setting, unlike the famous Meccan classification.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r9.anchor: Evvelkinde bilfiil kabirlere kadar gidilmemiş, sade kabirlerde bulunan ölülerin nam ve adedi anılarak tefâhur olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r10.speaker: Übey b. Ka‘b
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r10.claim: Ubay reports that the saying about a person with two valleys of wealth longing for a third, and being filled only by earth, was once recited as Quran until this surah came; God accepts the repentance of the penitent.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r10.anchor: Buhârî, Übey b. Ka‘b radıyallâhu anh’tan tahric eylemişlerdir; demiştir ki: “Biz لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r11.speaker: Abdullah b. Şihhir
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r11.claim: He reports that the Prophet explained a person's real wealth as what he gives away, consumes, or wears out; Tirmidhi grades the report hasan and sahih.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r11.anchor: Tirmizî ve İbn Cerîr Abdullah b. Şihhir’den tahric eylemişlerdir ki; müşârün ileyh Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’nin huzûruna varmış

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r12.speaker: İbn Cerîr
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r12.claim: Ibn Jarir infers from the Prophet's recitation followed by the saying that wealth rivalry is intended by takathur.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r12.anchor: İbn Cerîr de der ki: “Resûlullah’ın أَلْهَىٰكُمُ okuyup da akabinde öyle buyurması ‘tekâsür’ün mal tekâsürü olduğunu iş‘ar eder.”

ELMALILI:102:1-5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r13.claim: Some exegetes understand rivalry in numbers from the occasion reports and others rivalry in wealth from the prophetic report; combining both best fits the verse's unrestricted wording and 57:20.
ELMALILI:102:1-5/r13.anchor: ikisini de cem‘etmek âyetin ıtlâkına daha muvâfık ve evvelâ beyan olunan îzâha ve Sûre-i Hadid âyetine de mutabıktır.

ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r1.claim: The author classifies the preceding account as another instance of the same issue, then turns to God's command to recount blessings.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r1.anchor: rivayet de bu cümledendir. وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ

ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r2.claim: The explanation of 93:11 allows declaring God's blessings through obedience and good character when others may follow one's example.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r2.anchor: insanın başkaları tarafından kendisine iktidâ olunacağını zannettiği takdirde tâat ve mehâsin-i ahlâk ile tahdîs-i nimet olmak üzere iftihar etmesi câiz olduğuna dair söz geçmişti

ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r3.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r3.claim: Razi's principle is that rivalry in genuine happiness is not blameworthy; the author concludes that competition in knowledge, obedience, and praiseworthy character is commendable.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r3.anchor: ilimde, tâatte, ahlâk-ı hamîdede tekâsür memduh ve mahmuddur.

ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r4.claim: Competition in good works is commanded and encouraged by the commands to race and vie in good deeds.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r4.anchor: Hayrâtta müsabaka, yarış yalnız câiz olmakla kalmaz aynı zamanda سَابِقُوا emirleriyle me’mûrun bih olduğunda da şüphe yoktur

ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r5.claim: Even good deeds must be distinguished from showing off and pride; their weight depends more on sincerity and quality than sheer quantity.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r5.anchor: Zira hayır ve güzel amellerin güzelliği ve mîzanda ağır gelmesi

ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r6.claim: Blameworthy takathur is worldly rivalry that distracts from good works and contains a form of idle play.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#2/r6.anchor: Burada mezmum olan tekâsür de o gibi güzel amellerden alıkoyan ve mâhiyetinde bir nevi lehv bulunan tekâsürdür.

ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#3/r1.claim: The endpoint clause may attach to takathur or ilhā: people multiplied until visiting graves, were distracted into grave-boasting, or stayed distracted until death or grave-punishment.

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.claim: Reports on grave visitation establish its legitimacy, wisdom, timing, method, and etiquette.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r1.anchor: ziyâret-i kubûrun da meşrûiyetini, hikmetini, zamanını, usul ve âdâbını göstermektedir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.claim: Visitation does not entail asking the dead for help or invoking them; visitors greet them and ask Allah for safety for living and dead alike.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r2.anchor: ölülerden bir şey istemek, “yetiş yâ fülân” gibi istimdad etmek yoktur

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.claim: Visitors may recite Qur'an and dedicate its reward, while seeking Allah's will and preparing in complete faith for their own death.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r3.anchor: Kur’an okuyup sevâbını hediye etmek ve bilhassa geridekilerin de onlara iltihak edeceğini düşünerek

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.claim: The visit should prompt reflection on resurrection, judgment, the scales, and the destinations of deeds, strengthening resolve for faith and righteous action over rivalry and accumulation.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r4.anchor: bütün kalbiyle âhireti, sonunda o kabirlere gidileceği ve o kabirlerin deşileceği

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.claim: The dead have returned or been returned to Allah and enter their final states according to their standing before Him.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r5.anchor: Ölenler, indallah mertebelerine göre ya îşe-i râzıyeye

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.claim: A prophetic report says a person will be resurrected with those he loves, so those who love the good join the good and those who love evil join the evil.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r6.anchor: اَلْمَرْءُ مَعَ مَنْ أَحَبَّ sevdikleriyle haşrolunacaklarından iyileri sevenler iyilerle

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.claim: Love is valuable when it is for Allah and follows the command to follow the Prophet.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r7.anchor: Sevginin kıymeti de وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَشَدُّ حُبًّۭا لِّلَّهِ

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.claim: The dead have passed on: their deeds are theirs and yours are yours, so boasting or competing over them has no point.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r8.anchor: Onların kazancı kendilerine, sizin kazancınız sizedir; siz onların amellerinden mes’ul olacak değilsinizdir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.claim: Worship and seeking aid belong to Allah; helping people for Allah is praised, while begging people is blameworthy, and asking the dead is especially unfitting.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r9.anchor: ibadet ve isti‘âne ise ancak Allah’adır. Allah için halka i‘âne memduh

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.claim: One benefits from the deceased by reflecting on their lives and works and keeping their good example alive.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r10.anchor: Onlardan istifade onların ahvâl ve sîretlerini düşünerek ilmî, amelî eserlerinden

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.speaker: İbn Âbidîn
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.claim: Saints differ in their nearness to Allah, and visitors benefit in proportion to their own knowledge and insight into them.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r11.anchor: Onun için İbn Âbidîn [6053] rahmetullâhi aleyh

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.claim: A grave visit can affect a person like reading a book, awakening memories and reflection.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r12.anchor: Bir kabri ziyaretle bir kitap okur gibi tefekkürün uyandıracağı hatıralara göre bir tesir alması

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.claim: The best visit awakens the afterlife through tenderness of heart and sends the visitor back to life resolved to spend the remaining years in good works.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r13.anchor: âhiret hissini duyup o intibah ile hayâta dönmek ve gaflet perdesini sıyırıp kalan ömrünü hayr u hasenât ile

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.claim: A hadith says grave visitation reminds people of the afterlife.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r14.anchor: hadîs-i şerifte buna “çünkü o size âhireti tezekkür ettirir” diye tenbih buyurulmuştur

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.claim: Visiting graves to boast and compete reverses their proper lesson and expresses extreme hardheartedness and heedlessness, prompting the rebuke of 102:1–2.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r15.anchor: tefâhur gurûruyla tekâsür için yapmak kasvetin, gafletin son derecesi olduğundan dolayı

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.claim: On a literal reading, competition may end when graves are visited, or grave visitation itself may end worldly greed.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r16.anchor: yani kabirleri ziyaret ettiğiniz zaman o tekâsür ve ilhâ kalmadı

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.claim: Exegetes generally take grave visitation here as a metaphor for death, since death certainly ends competition.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r17.anchor: müfessirîn bu takdirde kabir ziyareti hakikat mânasına olmayıp ölümden kinaye olacağını söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.claim: Seeing a dead person, attending burial, or later visiting a grave can awaken reflection in receptive hearts, but this is not universal and is derivative of death.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r18.anchor: kalbi olanlara bu intibah ve tezkir hükmü inkişaf etmez değil ise de, bu umûmî ve kat‘î olmadığı gibi

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.claim: If literal visitation were intended, the wording would encourage a required or recommended practice, conflicting with the following rebuke.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r19.anchor: memnû‘ve mezmum değil, kelâmın sevki gayeye müteveccih

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.claim: The passage's purpose is to rebuke heedlessness and rivalry, not to promote grave visitation; this resolves the tension with the following prohibition.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r20.anchor: kelâmın mâ-sîka-lehi ziyâret-i kubûr değil ilhâ ve tekâsür ile tevbihtir

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.claim: The warning can mean that rivalry deludes people until their souls leave and their bodies enter the graves.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r21.anchor: Tekâsür sizleri öyle iğfal etti ki tâ canlarınız çıkıncaya, tenleriniz kabirlere girinceye kadar

ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.claim: The rebuke warns people not to waste worldly life in rivalry; they will learn the gravity and outcome of their heedlessness later.
ELMALILI:102:1-5#5/r22.anchor: sonu kabre varan dünyada ehem olan vazifeyi unutup da boş, fâni şeylerle eğlenip oyalanmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r1.claim: Takathur means an obsessive contest to amass and boast in whatever each age prizes—wealth, children, helpers—without higher purpose or moral responsibility; it can be individual or social.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r1.anchor: yüksek bir amaç gütmeden, neden niçin demeden mal, evlât, yardımcı ve hizmetçi gibi her devrin telakkisine göre çokluğuyla övünülen şeyleri büyük bir tutkuyla durmadan çoğaltma yarışına girişmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r2.claim: Though it describes pre-Islamic Arab attitudes, the warning is universal; a modern secular worldview of endless production, consumption, profit, and wealth is a contemporary example.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r2.anchor: çağımızda bazı ülke ve toplumlarda hâkim maneviyattan yoksun seküler zihniyet de durmadan üretmek, tüketip tekrar üretmek, kârı ve serveti sınırsızca çoğaltmak şeklinde bir dünya görüşünü içerir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r3.claim: Removing spiritual and moral values from this race produces injustice from personal to international relations, using economic, political, and communication power and generating global problems.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r3.anchor: bireysel ilişkilerden uluslar arası ilişkilere kadar uzanan bir haksızlık ve adaletsizlik düzeni doğurmakta ve nihayet dünyayı “global” sorunlar alanı haline getirmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r4.claim: The surah uses the arrogant Meccan elite to expose a basic human problem and its heavy cost.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r4.anchor: Mekke’nin burnu büyük eşrafının tutumları üzerinden temel bir insanlık sorununa ve bunun ağır bedeline dikkat çekilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.claim: Even if reports describe a specific occasion, the general target is human boasting in abundant wealth, offspring, and supporters; true superiority appears in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:102:1/r7.anchor: genel anlamda insan fıtratındaki mal, evlât ve taraftarların çokluğu ile övünme vb. davranışlar eleştirilmekte, gerçek üstünlüğün âhirette ortaya çıkacağı belirtilmektedir

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.speaker: ابن بريدة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the Ansar tribes Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith competed by boasting about their living members, then went to the graves and boasted of the dead; the surah was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في قبيلتين من الأنصار في بني حارثة وبني الحرث تفاخروا وتكاثروا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.speaker: علي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Muslims doubted punishment in the grave until the passage from “competition distracts you” through “then you will know” was revealed regarding that punishment.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234#2/r2.anchor: كنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت ﴿ ألهاكم التكاثر ﴾ إلى ﴿ ثم كلا سوف تعلمون ﴾ في عذاب القبر

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī say the passage concerns Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm competing over which clan had more notables, then counting their dead at the graves; Banū Sahm had more.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في حيين من قريش: بني عبد مناف وبني سهم كان بينهم لحاء فتعاند السادة والأشراف أيهم أكثر

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.claim: Qatāda offers another view: the verse concerns Jews boasting that one group outnumbered another until death carried them off in error.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p464/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: نزلت في اليهود، قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان وبنو فلان أكثر من بني فلان، ألهاهم ذلك حتى ماتوا ضلالا.

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.claim: One interpretation says greed for wealth distracts people until death and only then do they bequeath funds for alms and pilgrimage.
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r1.anchor: الحرص على المال وطلب تكثيره حتى منعتم الحقوق المالية

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.claim: Another interpretation says accumulation distracts from religion; people have hearts like stones that soften only when they visit graves, though even this slight response is inadequate.
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r2.anchor: فلا تلتفتون إلى الدين ، بل قلوبكم كأنها أحجار لا تنكسر

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r3.claim: Leaving the object of distracted unspecified makes the rebuke broader, covering neglect of remembrance, obligations, recommended acts, knowledge, worship, reflection, and contemplation.

RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.claim: Read in context, accumulation distracts either from preparing for the Calamity before death or from remembering the grave until people reach it.
RAZI-FULL:v32p74/r4.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر عن التدبر في أمر القارعة والاستعداد لها قبل الموت

TABATABAI:102:8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:102:8/r1.speaker: أبو بريدة
TABATABAI:102:8/r1.claim: One reported occasion says the chapter came down about a clan of the Ansar competing in boasts.
TABATABAI:102:8/r1.anchor: وقيل نزلت في فخذ من الأنصار تفاخروا عن أبي بريدة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.speaker: أبو بريدة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.claim: Although many call the surah Meccan, al-Alusi chooses Medina based on Abu Burayda's report: two Ansari clans boast of living ancestors, then go to the graves to boast of the dead, prompting its revelation. A report from Ubayy says the warning about Adam's desire for a third valley continued until the surah descended; Ali says it ended doubts about grave punishment, which al-Alusi takes as Medinan evidence because that punishment is mentioned in a Medinan context.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r1.anchor: عن أبي بريدة فيها قال نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الانصار في بني حارثة وبني الحرث تفاخروا وتكاثروا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r2.claim: The surah has eight verses unanimously; reports also call it equal to a thousand verses, and its connection with the preceding surah is evident.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r2.anchor: وآيها ثمان بالاتفاق وهي تعدل ألف آية من القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.claim: Ibn al-Milq explains the thousand-verse merit as one sixth of the Qur'an's roughly 6,200 verses: al-Ghazali's six aims include knowledge of the return to God, which this surah contains. Al-Alusi says the matter lies beyond this calculation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p223/r3.anchor: ذكر ناصر الدين بن الميلق في سر ذلك أن القرآن ستة آلاف ومائتا آية وكسر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p518/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p518/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p518/r12.claim: The ending returns to the opening with a subtle warning: knowing every pleasure will be questioned restrains indulgence, even in permissible things, all the more so in disliked or forbidden things, especially when the questioner is the majestic King and questioning can lead to punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p518/r12.anchor: العاقل إذا علم أن بين يديه سؤالا عن كل ما يتلذذ به علم أنه يعوقه ذلك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p236/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p236/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p236/r1.claim: The address concerns those whom worldly accumulation distracted from preparing for the afterlife.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p236/r1.anchor: الذين ألهاهم التكاثر في أعراض الدنيا عن اتزود لأخراهم

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r1.speaker: جميع المفسرين والبخاري
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r1.claim: All exegetes cited say al-Takathur is Meccan, while al-Bukhari says it is Medinan.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول جميع المفسرين . وقال البخاري : مدنية

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says the connection with the preceding surah is evident.

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil report a rivalry between Banu Sahm and Banu Abd Manaf: they counted living notables, then the dead; Abd Manaf won among the living and Sahm among the dead because it had been larger in pre-Islamic times.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r3.anchor: أنه فيما روى الكلبي ومقاتل : كان بين بني سهم وبين بني عبد مناف لحاء ، فتعادوا الأشراف الأحياء

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r4.claim: Qatada says the surah was revealed concerning Jews who claimed that they outnumbered one tribe and another tribe outnumbered a third.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة : نزلت في اليهود ، قالوا : نحن أكثر من بني فلان وبنو فلان أكثر من بني فلان

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the surah was revealed concerning a clan of the Ansar.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : نزلت في بطن من الأنصار

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r6.claim: Alhakum means “occupied you”; in the account of al-Kalbi and Muqatil, rivalry over living people expanded to include the dead at the graves.

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.claim: Calling their mention of the dead “visiting the graves” is a sarcastic way to describe the rivals' conduct.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r7.anchor: عبر عن بلوغهم ذكر الموتى بزيارة المقابر تهكما بهم

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r8.claim: The majority read أَلْهَاكُمُ as a declarative statement.

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة، والكلبي ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Muawiya, Abu Imran al-Jawni, Abu Salih, Malik ibn Dinar, Abu al-Jawza, others, and reports from al-Kalbi and Yaqub have the stretched interrogative reading.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r9.anchor: وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة : بالمد على الاستفهام

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r10.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r10.claim: Abu Bakr, Ibn Abbas, al-Shaʿbi, Abu al-Aliya, Ibn Abi Ablah, and al-Kisaʾi in one transmission have a two-hamza interrogative reading.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r10.anchor: وعن أبي بكر الصديق وابن عباس أيضا والشعبي وأبي العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي في رواية : أألهاكم

ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r11.claim: The interrogative readings express rebuke and make the ugliness of the conduct explicit, though Abu Hayyan says this sense does not readily fit the wording زُرْتُم.
ABUHAYYAN:102:1/r11.anchor: ومعنى الاستفهام : التوبيخ والتقرير على قبح فعلهم ؛ وهذا معنى ينبو عنه لفظ زرتم

ALUSI:102:1/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي هلال
ALUSI:102:1/r1.claim: The Companions called this sūra al-Maqbara, the Graveyard Sūra.
ALUSI:102:1/r1.anchor: وكان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعد بن أبي هلال يسمونها المقبرة

ALUSI:102:1/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r2.speaker: أبو حيان والجلال السيوطي
ALUSI:102:1/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says all exegetes regard the sūra as Meccan; al-Suyūṭī calls that the more common view.
ALUSI:102:1/r2.anchor: قال أبو حيان عند جميع المفسرين وقال الجلال السيوطي على الأشهر

ALUSI:102:1/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r3.speaker: أبو بريدة
ALUSI:102:1/r3.claim: Abū Burayda reports that two Ansari clans, Banū Ḥāritha and Banū al-Ḥārith, boasted of living members, then their dead, prompting the revelation.
ALUSI:102:1/r3.anchor: عن أبي بريدة فيها قال نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار في بني حارثة وبني الحرث

ALUSI:102:1/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:1/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī selects the Medinan view, citing the Ansari occasion and other evidence for a Medinan revelation.
ALUSI:102:1/r4.anchor: ويدل لكونها مدنية وهو المختار ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي بريدة

ALUSI:102:1/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI:102:1/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says they had treated the saying about Adam's two valleys of wealth, desire for a third, and a belly filled only by earth as Qur'an until this sūra came; God accepts the repentance of the repentant.
ALUSI:102:1/r5.anchor: عن أبي ابن كعب قال كنا نرى هذا من القرآن لو أن لابن آدم

ALUSI:102:1/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r6.speaker: علي
ALUSI:102:1/r6.claim: ʿAlī reports that they continued to doubt punishment in the grave until this sūra was revealed; al-Ālūsī adds that grave punishment is mentioned only in Medinan material.
ALUSI:102:1/r6.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه مازلنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت ألهاكم التكاثر

ALUSI:102:1/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:1/r7.claim: The sūra has eight verses by consensus.

ALUSI:102:1/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI:102:1/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar transmits the Prophet's question whether anyone can recite a thousand verses daily and his suggestion to recite this sūra.
ALUSI:102:1/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ألا يستطيع أحدكم

ALUSI:102:1/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r9.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ALUSI:102:1/r9.claim: ʿUmar reports that whoever recites a thousand verses meets God smiling; the Prophet recited this sūra and said it equals a thousand verses.
ALUSI:102:1/r9.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من قرأ

ALUSI:102:1/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r10.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ALUSI:102:1/r10.claim: Ibn al-Milq explains the thousand-verse merit as one-sixth of the Qur'an's aims: knowing God, the straight path, return to God, the obedient, deniers, and stages of the way; al-Ālūsī says the true reason is beyond this.
ALUSI:102:1/r10.anchor: وذكر ناصر الدين بن الميلق في سر ذلك أن القرآن ستة آلاف ومائتا آية وكسر

ALUSI:102:1/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:1/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's connection to the preceding sūra is evident.
ALUSI:102:1/r11.anchor: والأمر والله تعالى أعلم وراء ذلك ومناسبتها لما قبلها ظاهرة

ALUSI:102:1/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:1/r12.claim: Lahw originally means heedlessness, then came to mean anything distracting; convention narrows it to a pleasurable distraction, close to play. Here it makes people heedless.
ALUSI:102:1/r12.anchor: وأصل اللهو الغفلة ثم شاعر في كل شاغر وخصه العرف بالشاغل الذي يسر المرء

ALUSI:102:1/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r13.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI:102:1/r13.claim: Al-Rāghib defines lahw as what distracts one from what matters and concerns; al-Ālūsī applies the sense of heedlessness here.
ALUSI:102:1/r13.anchor: وقال الراغب اللهو ما يشغلك عما يعني ويهم وقيل ليس بذاك المراد به هنا الغفلة

ALUSI:102:1/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:1/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:1/r14.claim: Takāthur is competing and boasting over numbers, each group claiming to be more numerous.
ALUSI:102:1/r14.anchor: التباري في الكثرة والتباهي بها بأن يقول هؤلاء نحن أكثر وهؤلاء نحن أكثر

ALUSI:102:2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:102:2/r6.claim: Boasting distracts from religion, the most important concern; suppressing the object of distraction magnifies it and intensifies the blame, condemning anything that distracts.
ALUSI:102:2/r6.anchor: وحذف الملهى عنه للتعظيم المأخوذ من الإبهام بالحذف والمبالغة في الذم

ALUSI:102:2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI:102:2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan explain that wealth and children distract people until death, with grave-visiting standing for dying.
ALUSI:102:2/r7.anchor: وصدره قد أخرجه ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس وهو ابن أبي حاتم وابن أبي شيبة عن الحسن

ALUSI:102:2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI:102:2/r12.claim: Abū Muslim says God addresses the sūra to unbelievers on Judgment Day, reproaching them for graves they had already visited; al-Ālūsī finds this astonishing.
ALUSI:102:2/r12.anchor: قول أبي مسلم أن الله عز وجل يتكلم بهذه السورة يوم القيامة تعييرا للكفار

ALUSI:102:2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة
ALUSI:102:2/r16.claim: These readers lengthen the initial hamza in alhākum as an interrogative.
ALUSI:102:2/r16.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة آلهاكم بالمد على الاستفهام

ALUSI:102:2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:102:2/r17.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي
ALUSI:102:2/r17.claim: These readers use two hamzas in a question; the interrogative is for affirmation.
ALUSI:102:2/r17.anchor: وروى عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وابن عباس

BAGHAWI:102:1/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:1/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:102:1/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Takāthur is Meccan and has eight verses.

BAGHAWI:102:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:1/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:102:1/r2.claim: Boasting and competing over wealth and numbers distract people from obeying their Lord and from what saves them from His anger.
BAGHAWI:102:1/r2.anchor: بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة ربكم

BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.claim: Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports from his father that the Prophet explained a person's wealth is only what he consumes, wears out, or gives away and sends ahead.
BAGHAWI:102:2/r4.anchor: عن مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير ،   عن أبيه

BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's saying that three follow the dead, but family and wealth return while deeds remain.
BAGHAWI:102:2/r5.anchor: أنس بن مالك يقول :  "  قال رسول الله

BAYDAWI:102:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:102:1/r1.claim: The sūra's place of revelation is disputed, and it has eight verses.
BAYDAWI:102:1/r1.anchor: سورة التكاثر مختلف فيها ،   وآيها ثماني آيات

BAYDAWI:102:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:102:1/r2.claim: Alhākum means it occupied or distracted you; the root conveys turning toward pastime and derives from lahā, to be heedless.
BAYDAWI:102:1/r2.anchor: ألهاكم : شغلكم ،   وأصله الصرف إلى اللهو ،   منقول من لها إذا غفل

BAYDAWI:102:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:1/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:102:1/r3.anchor: منقول من لها إذا غفل .   التكاثر : التباهي بالكثرة

BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.claim: The object of distraction—the religious matters that concern them—is omitted for grandeur and emphasis.
BAYDAWI:102:2/r4.anchor: وإنما حذف المنهي عنه وهو ما يعنيهم من أمر الدين للتعظيم والمبالغة

BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.claim: Another view takes the rivalry over wealth and children as lasting until death and burial, wasting life that should have prepared for the afterlife; visiting graves means dying.
BAYDAWI:102:2/r5.anchor: ألهاكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد إلى أن متم وقبرتم مضيعين أعماركم في طلب الدنيا

BIQAI:102:1/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r1.claim: After al-Qāriʿa establishes the Hour, divides people into wretched and happy, and ends with the wretched, this sūra opens with the cause of misery to warn listeners away from it.
BIQAI:102:1/r1.anchor: لما أثبت في القارعة أمر الساعة

BIQAI:102:1/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r2.claim: Alhākum means that this rivalry deeply distracted nearly everyone.
BIQAI:102:1/r2.anchor: أي أغفلكم - إلا النادر منكم - غفلة عظيمة

BIQAI:102:1/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r3.claim: Al-takāthur is boasting over plentiful, perishable worldly goods such as wealth, rank, and children.
BIQAI:102:1/r3.anchor: وهو المباهاة والمفاخرة بكثرة الأعراض الفانية

BIQAI:102:1/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r4.claim: The rivalry consumes effort in gathering and distracts from death, the afterlife, true religion, remembrance of God, and competing in saving acts.

BIQAI:102:1/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r5.claim: Ignorance born of desire, self-love, and love of ease keeps people from submitting, so their scales grow light.
BIQAI:102:1/r5.anchor: لأنكم لا تسلمون بما غلب عليكم من الجهل الذي سببه شهوة النفس وحب الراحة فخفت موازينكم

BIQAI:102:1/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r6.claim: The object of distraction is left unstated to magnify what they neglect and suggest nothing is more grievous to neglect.
BIQAI:102:1/r6.anchor: وحذف هذا الشيء الملهو عنه لتعظيمه والدلالة على أنه ليس غيره مما يؤسف على اللهو عنه

BIQAI:102:2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:102:2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the sūra to the preceding al-Qāriʿa: rivalry in numbers, kin, and family distracts from preparing for its terrors and is followed by threats.
BIQAI:102:2/r6.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

DURR:102:1/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:102:1/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Sūrat al-Takāthur was revealed in Mecca.
DURR:102:1/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : نزلت بمكة سورة { ألهاكم التكاثر } .

DURR:102:1/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r2.claim: The Prophet asks whether anyone can recite a thousand verses daily; after they doubt anyone can, he asks whether one can recite Sūrat al-Takāthur.
DURR:102:1/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «ألا يستطيع أحدكم أن يقرأ ألف آية في كل يوم

DURR:102:1/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r3.speaker: أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal reports that the Companions called the sura “al-Mughira.”
DURR:102:1/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي هلال رضي الله عنه قال : كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسمون { ألهاكم التكاثر } المغيرة .

DURR:102:1/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r4.claim: Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir found the Prophet reciting the sura (another wording says it had just been revealed); the Prophet says one's lasting wealth is what one consumed, wore out, or gave away.
DURR:102:1/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الشخير رضي الله عنه قال : انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ { ألهاكم التكاثر }

DURR:102:1/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r5.claim: The Prophet teaches that a person's wealth is only what was consumed, worn out, or given ahead for the afterlife.
DURR:102:1/r5.anchor: عن مطرف ، عن أبيه قال : لما أنزلت { ألهاكم التكاثر } قال : رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «يقول ابن آدم : مالي مالي

DURR:102:1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra's version says a servant has only three parts of his wealth: what he eats and consumes, wears and wears out, or gives as charity; the rest is left to others.
DURR:102:1/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «يقول العبد : مالي مالي ، وإنما له من ماله ثلاثة

DURR:102:1/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r7.claim: Al-Hasan's version says the son of Adam owns only what he consumed, wore out, or gave and sent ahead.
DURR:102:1/r7.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «يقول ابن آدم : مالي

DURR:102:1/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r8.claim: The Prophet invites people to hear the sura, saying whoever weeps enters Paradise and whoever cannot weep should feign tears; al-Bayhaqi weakened the report.
DURR:102:1/r8.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال : «قال لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : إني قارئ عليكم سورة { ألهاكم التكاثر }

DURR:102:1/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
DURR:102:1/r9.claim: Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir says he came upon the Prophet in prayer, reciting Sūrat al-Takāthur through its end.
DURR:102:1/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الشخير رضي الله عنه قال : أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي ، وهو يقرأ { ألهاكم التكاثر } حتى ختمها

DURR:102:1/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r10.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR:102:1/r10.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says they once regarded a saying about Adam's two valleys of wealth, his desire for a third, and a belly filled only by dust as Qur'an, until this sura was revealed through its end.
DURR:102:1/r10.anchor: عن أبيّ بن كعب رضي الله عنه قال : كنا نرى هذا من القرآن : لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال

DURR:102:1/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR:102:1/r11.claim: Qatada says people boasted that their clan outnumbered another, distracting them in rivalry until they died astray.
DURR:102:1/r11.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه { ألهاكم التكاثر } قال : قالوا : نحن أكثر من بني فلان

DURR:102:1/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR:102:1/r12.claim: Qatada says the sura was revealed concerning the Jews.
DURR:102:1/r12.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ألهاكم التكاثر } قال : نزلت في اليهود .

DURR:102:1/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r13.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:102:1/r13.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says the sura was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave.
DURR:102:1/r13.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : نزلت { ألهاكم التكاثر } في عذاب القبر .

DURR:102:1/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:102:1/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the rivalry as concerning wealth and children.
DURR:102:1/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ألهاكم التكاثر } قال : في الأموال والأولاد .

DURR:102:1/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:102:1/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:102:1/r15.claim: The Prophet says he fears rivalry and deliberate wrongdoing for his community more than poverty and mistakes; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:102:1/r15.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «ما أخشى عليكم الفقر ، ولكن أخشى عليكم التكاثر

IBNASHUR:102:1/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r1.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
IBNASHUR:102:1/r1.claim: Al-Alusi reports from Ibn Abi Hatim, from Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal, that the Prophet's Companions called this chapter al-Maqbarah.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r1.anchor: قال الآلوسي أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن أبي هلال : كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسمونها { المقبرة }

IBNASHUR:102:1/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r2.claim: Most Qur'an codices and commentaries call it Surat al-Takathur; Tirmidhi uses that title, as do some old Qayrawan codices, while other codices and Bukhari call it Surat Alhakum.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r2.anchor: وسميت في معظم المصاحف ومعظم التفاسير { سورة التكاثر } وكذلك عنونها الترمذي في جامعه

IBNASHUR:102:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r3.claim: Most authorities regard the chapter as Meccan, and Ibn ʿAtiyya says he knows no disagreement; Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil report a dispute between Quraysh clans as its occasion.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r3.anchor: وهي مكية عند الجمهور قال ابن عطية : هي مكية لا أعلم فيها خلافا

IBNASHUR:102:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل
IBNASHUR:102:1/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil say the chapter arose from a boastful competition between Banu ʿAbd Manaf and Banu Sahm in Mecca.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل : إنها نزلت في مفاخرة جرت بين بني عبد مناف وبني سهم

IBNASHUR:102:1/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r5.speaker: السيوطي
IBNASHUR:102:1/r5.claim: Al-Suyuti's preferred view in al-Itqan is that the chapter is Medinan, citing a report about Ansari clans and a hadith from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r5.anchor: وفي الإتقان : المختار : أنها مدنية . قال : ويدل له ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم أنها نزلت في قبيلتين من الأنصار تفاخروا

IBNASHUR:102:1/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNASHUR:102:1/r6.claim: Ubayy reports the Prophet's saying that Adam's child would want a second valley of gold, be filled only by earth, and can repent; Ubayy says they thought this saying Qur'an until the chapter descended.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r6.anchor: وما أخرجه البخاري عن أبي بن كعب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لو أن لابن آدم واديا من ذهب أحب أن يكون له واديان

IBNASHUR:102:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAshur says Ubayy's report does not establish a Medinan date: we could mean Muslims generally, who stopped treating the saying as Qur'an after clarification.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r7.anchor: وليس في كلام أبي دليل ناهض إذ يجوز أن يريد بضمير كنا المسلمين ، أي كان من سبق منهم يعد ذلك من القرآن حتى نزلت سورة التكاثر

IBNASHUR:102:1/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r8.claim: He prefers a Meccan date because the chapter's themes and severe threats suit a group of polytheists, not the Muslims of that period.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r8.anchor: والذي يظهر من معاني السورة وغلظة وعيدها أنها مكية وأن المخاطب بها فريق من المشركين

IBNASHUR:102:1/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r9.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي والقرطبي وابن عباس
IBNASHUR:102:1/r9.claim: The reported occasion is a tally of chiefs and notables by Banu ʿAbd Manaf and Banu Sahm; Banu Sahm outnumbered them by three households in pre-Islamic times.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r9.anchor: أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم من قريش تفاخروا فتعادوا السادة والأشراف من أيهم أكثر عددا فكثر بنو عبد مناف بنو سهم بثلاثة أبيات

IBNASHUR:102:1/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r10.speaker: أبو بريدة الجرمي
IBNASHUR:102:1/r10.claim: Abu Buraydah al-Jarmi reports that the Ansari clans Banu Harithah and Banu al-Harith boasted of living members, then pointed to their dead in graves, prompting revelation.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي بريدة الجرمي قال : نزلت في قبيلتين من الأنصار بني حارثة وبني الحارث تفاخروا وتكاثروا بالأحياء

IBNASHUR:102:1/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r11.claim: On the Meccan chronology, this is the sixteenth chapter revealed, after al-Kawthar and before al-Maʿun; it has eight verses.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r11.anchor: وقد عدت السادسة عشرة في ترتيب نزول السور ، ونزلت بعد سورة الكوثر وقبل سورة الماعون بناء على أنها مكية . وعدد آيتها ثمان

IBNASHUR:102:1/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r12.claim: The chapter rebukes neglect of Qur'anic guidance for wealth, accumulation, and ancestral boasting through death; it warns, urges reflection on salvation, and reminds them of resurrection and accountability for gratitude.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r12.anchor: اشتملت على التوبيخ على اللهو عن النظر في دلائل القرآن ودعوة الإسلام بإيثار المال والتكاثر به والتفاخر بالأسلاف

IBNASHUR:102:1/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r13.claim: ألهاكم means it occupied and diverted you from what you ought to attend to; amusement is an occupation that blocks an important aim.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r13.anchor: { ألهاكم } أي شغلكم عما يجب عليكم الاشتغالُ به لأن اللهو شغل يصرف عن تحصيل أمرٍ مهم

IBNASHUR:102:1/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r14.claim: التكاثر is competing to accumulate something valued in quantity, such as wealth, children, or allies used for prestige.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r14.anchor: و { التكاثر } : تفاعل في الكثْر أي التباري في الإِكثار من شيء مرغوب في كثرته

IBNASHUR:102:1/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r15.claim: The word includes rivalry in wealth and in numbers of children or allies, as people boast that their wealth and children protect them from punishment.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r15.anchor: فمنه تكاثر في الأموال ، ومنه تكاثر في العَدد من الأولاد والأحلاف للاعتزاز بهم

IBNASHUR:102:1/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r16.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR:102:1/r16.claim: Al-Aʿsha's verse contrasts being outnumbered with the fact that prestige belongs to the larger group, illustrating takathur as competition in numbers.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r16.anchor:
وقال الأعشى :
ولستَ بالأكْثر منهم حَصًى *** وإنما العِزة للكَاثر

IBNASHUR:102:1/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
IBNASHUR:102:1/r17.claim: Ibn al-Shikhkhir reports the Prophet reciting the chapter and explaining that a person's wealth is only what he consumes, wears out, or gives away in charity.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r17.anchor: روى مسلم عن عبد الله بن الشِّخِّير قال :

IBNASHUR:102:1/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r18.claim: The hadith offers one meaning of competing over possessions that the verse can bear, prompted by that moment's admonition.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r18.anchor: فهذا جارٍ مجرى التفسير لمعنى من معاني التكاثر اقتضاه حال الموعظة ساعتئذ وتحتمله الآية

IBNASHUR:102:1/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r19.claim: The address targets polytheists, especially their affluent leaders, because of the severe threats and because such conduct was not a Muslim trait then.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r19.anchor: والخطاب للمشركين بقرينة غلظة الوعيد بقوله : { كلا سوف تعلمون ثم كلا سوف تعلمون }

IBNASHUR:102:1/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r20.claim: The intended addressees are wealthy chiefs who chose luxury over hearing Muhammad's call and obstructed ordinary people; the unspoken object of diversion is plainly Qur'an, reflection, and fair acceptance.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r20.anchor: والمراد بالخطاب : سادتُهم وأهلُ الثراء منهم لقوله : { ثم لتسئلن يومئذٍ عن النعيم }

IBNASHUR:102:1/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r21.claim: The object of ألهاكم is omitted because its reference to the Qur'an, reflection, and accepting its truth is evident; the past tense presents their distraction as accomplished.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r21.anchor: فلم يُذكَر المُلْهَى عنه لظهور أنه القرآن والتدبر فيه ، والإِنصاف بتصديقه

IBNASHUR:102:1/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:102:1/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:102:1/r22.claim: Although the rebuke addresses polytheists, believers too must avoid love of wealth distracting them from good and heed the risk of sudden death; another verse warns them about worldly rivalry.
IBNASHUR:102:1/r22.anchor: فلأن المسلمين يعلمون أن التلبس بشيء من هذا الخلق مذموم عند الله

IBNATIYYA:102:1/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya knows of no disagreement about that.
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r1.anchor: وهي مكية ، لا أعلم فيها خلافا

IBNATIYYA:102:1/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r2.claim: Alhākum means that worldly pleasures occupied and distracted you; the word is used of idle talk, sounds, and pleasure in women.
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r2.anchor: «ألهى » معناه : شغل بلذاته ، ومنه لهو الحديث والأصوات واللهو بالنساء

IBNATIYYA:102:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r3.claim: The statement is phrased as news but functions as censure, reproach, and lament.
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r3.anchor: وهذا خبر فيه تقريع وتوبيخ وتحسر

IBNATIYYA:102:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعمران الجوني وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿImrān al-Jawnī, and Abū Ṣāliḥ read it as an interrogative, aʾalhākum.
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعمران الجوني وأبو صالح : «أألهاكم » على الاستفهام

IBNATIYYA:102:1/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r5.claim: Takāthur is mutual boasting in wealth, children, and numbers generally, a habitual preoccupation of worldly people, Arab and non-Arab, except for learned and devout people.
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r5.anchor: و { التكاثر } هي المفاخرة بالأموال والأولاد والعدد جملة

IBNATIYYA:102:1/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r6.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r6.claim: Al-Aʿshā says might belongs to the numerous, illustrating how boasting treats numerical abundance as a source of status.
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r6.anchor: وقد قال الأعشى : [ السريع ] ولست بالأكثر منهم حصى

IBNATIYYA:102:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet’s teaching that one keeps only food consumed, clothes worn out, or charity sent ahead; another route is from Ibn al-Shikhkhīr.
IBNATIYYA:102:1/r7.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : «يقول ابن آدم : مالي مالي ، وهل لك من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت ، أو لبست فأبليت ، أو تصدقت فأمضيت

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Surat al-Takathur as Meccan.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r1.anchor: مقدمة السورة: تفسير سورة التكاثر وهي مكية .

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r2.claim: Love of worldly life, its pleasures, and its adornment distracted people from seeking and pursuing the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r2.anchor: يقول تعالى : شغلكم حب الدنيا ونعيمها وزهرتها عن طلب الآخرة وابتغائها ،

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet explains that rivalry distracted people from obedience until death came; Ibn Kathir cites it through Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam from his father.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } عن الطاعة ، { حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } حتى يأتيكم الموت

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r5.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says the rivalry concerns wealth and children.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } في الأموال والأولاد .

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r6.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab reports that they had regarded the saying about Adam's having a valley of gold as Quran until this sura was revealed.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r6.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك ، عن أبي بن كعب قال : كنا نرى هذا من القرآن حتى نزلت : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ }

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r7.claim: The Prophet describes the son of Adam's claim my wealth, my wealth, and says only what he eats, wears, or gives in charity truly remains his.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r7.anchor: عن أبيه قال : انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقول :  " { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } يقول ابن آدم : مالي مالي

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r8.claim: The Prophet says a servant has only three uses of wealth: food consumed, clothing worn out, or charity stored as lasting reward; the rest is left to others.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " يقول العبد : مالي مالي ؟ وإنما له من ماله ثلاث

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.claim: The Prophet says three follow the dead person—family, wealth, and deeds; the family and wealth return, while the deeds remain.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r9.anchor: سمع أنس بن مالك يقول : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " يتبع الميت ثلاثةٌ ، فيرجع اثنان ويبقى معه واحد

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r10.claim: The Prophet says that as the son of Adam ages, two traits persist: greed and hope.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r10.anchor: عن أنس : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :  " يهرم ابن آدم وتبقى منه اثنتان : الحرص والأمل "

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r11.speaker: الأحنف بن قيس
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r11.claim: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays tells a man that a dirham is truly his only when he spends it toward reward or in gratitude.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r11.anchor: الأحنف بن قيس{[30458]} - واسمه الضحاك - أنه رأى في يد رجل درهما فقال : لمن هذا الدرهم ؟ فقال الرجل : لي . فقال : إنما هو لك

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r12.speaker: الشاعر
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r12.claim: The poet's verse illustrates that money belongs to its holder when kept, but truly becomes his when spent.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r12.anchor: ثم أنشد الأحنف متمثلا قول الشاعر : أنتَ للمال إذا أمسكتَه *** فإذا أنفقتَه فالمالُ لَكْ

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.speaker: ابن بريدة
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.claim: Ibn Burayda says the verses were revealed about two Ansari tribes, Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith, who competed over living notable relatives and then boasted over the dead at their graves.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r13.anchor: عن ابن بريدة في قوله : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ } قال : نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار ، في بني حارثة وبني الحارث

IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.claim: Qatada says people boasted that they outnumbered other tribes, while their members continually died until all had become inhabitants of graves.
IBNKATHIR:102:1/r14.anchor: وقال قتادة : { أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ } كانوا يقولون : نحن أكثر من بني فلان
